chapters.title: Chapter 1759: Lady Khronisia’s Request
paragraphs: Bringing Meiko to the Tower turned out to be the right decision.
She got to meet some of Kent’s wives and everyone else living inside the Tower. Seeing the millions of people populating the various cities, she became a bit emotional.

After all, before she died during the Flame Era, she had been put in charge of an entire galaxy. While she had killed some of the high-ranking Flame Beasts and even the main threat, she knew that with her death, thousands had perished as well.
Seeing how peaceful life was inside the Tower, she knew that if a place like this had existed in the past, perhaps she wouldn’t have died so early.
She would have had more freedom to counter the threats without constantly worrying about the innocent people she was supposed to protect.
Seeing how much she loved the Tower, Kent decided to let her stay for a while. He had other obligations to attend to, so he left to address them.
After leaving, he appeared back on Planet Elyria-IV, where Lady Khronisia from the Blacksmith Association was waiting for him.

He had already received a quest to protect her on her journey back to her planet since she would come under attack. So he had asked her to wait after the auction while he dealt with the events involving the Fatty.

He had promised to meet her even before his memories of Fjorge returned to him. Now, he was even more eager since he would finally be making contact with a high-ranking member of the Blacksmith Association in the Immortal Realm.

Not many women entered the field of blacksmithing because it was traditionally considered a man’s profession. However, Fjorge, who had ventured deep into the world of blacksmithing, had encountered many legendary female blacksmiths and even worked alongside some of them. As such, Lady Khronisia had piqued his interest.
Now that he was free, he returned to Planet Elyria-IV and quickly contacted her. A few minutes later, they met in a restaurant to discuss why she had wanted to see him.
"Thank you for coming, Kent Madson," she said politely, looking at the man who had shaken the hearts of countless people during the auction five days earlier.
His name had already spread far and wide, causing billions to wonder what kind of existence he truly was. They had all witnessed him kill a Universal God despite not even reaching the Demigod stage.
That feat alone was beyond shocking, and now that she was sitting across from Kent, she couldn’t help but wonder who he really was.
Of course, she kept those thoughts to herself.
Kent merely smiled and replied, "I promised you, after all. So here I am, Lady Khronisia."
She nodded and went straight to the point.

"I didn’t call you here to waste your time, so I’ll be direct. I have been searching for you for quite some time because I need your help crafting a weapon that I plan to submit to the Association as my masterpiece before taking the Blacksmith God Trial and ascending.
It requires two important things. First, I need a Primordial Flame, which I already have. Second, I need an Absolute-grade Ice that possesses a true name.
I know it is a big request, but compared to you, almost everyone else on the Ice Dao Tablet is beyond my reach. You are the only one still in the Immortal Realm who possesses an ice with a true name.
So I humbly ask if you can spare a week of your time to assist me in crafting this once-in-a-lifetime weapon."
"Once-in-a-lifetime weapon, you say?" Kent smiled faintly, recalling the dagger he had crafted after spending ten years learning under Immortal Blacksmith Ricado.
The Midnight Dagger he created had become a symbol of his craftsmanship throughout the Immortal Realm.
Of course, he had gone on to forge many Immortal-grade weapons after creating the Midnight Dagger, but that one remained his masterpiece—not because it was the strongest or the best.
It was because it was the very first weapon he had designed and crafted entirely on his own, without Immortal Blacksmith Ricado’s guidance.
It was his first true work of craftsmanship. He had spent days perfecting the concept alone before even beginning to plan which materials would best bring his vision to life.
"First of all, I want to ask, how long have you been planning this craftsmanship of yours?"
Lady Khronisia blinked a few times, not expecting Kent to ask such a question. However, she answered anyway.
"About 12,000 years. A few years after I became an Immortal Blacksmith, I attended an auction and witnessed the sale of one of the legendary Ten Divine Zodiac Spears.

It was only for a few minutes, but I gained profound insight into the path of blacksmithing. Since then, I have been planning to create something similar, but mine would embody only the powers of Ice and Flame.
It took a long time to plan and gather the necessary resources, but I believe that with your Ice, I can craft a similar spear."
"I see. That is quite ambitious of you, Lady Khronisia." Kent chuckled softly before adding, "The Ten Divine Zodiac Spears were masterpieces created by the Zodiac Forgebinder during the Flame Era.

He forged them using Sacred Flames and imbued each one with the authority of one of his Ten Sacred Flames. In fact, history records that, aside from the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith, he was one of the greatest blacksmiths ever to live.
To think you aspire to craft something comparable to his work—I must say, you have both courage and ambition. I admire that, and because of it, I will help you. However, I have one request."
Hearing that he was willing to help, Lady Khronisia beamed with joy.
"As long as it is within my power to provide, I wouldn’t refuse any request from you."
"Good, because I want to see your blueprint and help you perfect it. However, instead of using a Primordial Flame, you will be using a Sacred Flame that I will provide."
"What...?"
Her eyes widened, and for a moment, she felt as though she had just heard the greatest joke in existence. However, when Kent ignited one of the Nirvana Flames, her expression instantly turned pale.
"This...?"
"It is one of the Nine Nirvana Flames. Though this is only a spark, I will soon obtain the real flame, and I plan on helping you forge the weapon with it.
I only ask that when it is time to inscribe the runes, you add these."
Kent flicked his hand, and three runes appeared in the air.
The moment Lady Khronisia saw the true runes, her eyes widened even further. In fact, she immediately jumped to her feet and moved closer to inspect them.
"Th-These are the Soul Awakening, Soul Dimension, and Soul Nourishing Runes," she blurted out. Had Kent not sealed their private room, everyone in the restaurant would have heard her.

"Yes. Yes, and yes." Kent nodded. "You originally planned to craft nothing more than an Immortal-grade Divine Weapon. However, with these runes, you will instead be forging an Immortal-grade Soul Weapon, one capable of housing a weapon spirit and continuing to grow stronger as time passes."
"But... but why would you do all this for me? I only needed your Ice element."
Kent laughed, poured himself a drink, and took a sip.

"Let’s just say I’m impressed by your idea. As someone who always wishes to see the very best in everything, I want you to have this opportunity to show the universe what you can do. Who knows, maybe the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith would notice your efforts and take you as his disciple."
Of course, Kent wasn’t doing this out of the goodness of his heart.
He needed this weapon to finally lure his stubborn hammer back to his side.

Yes, and yes." Kent nodded.
"You originally planned to craft nothing more than an Immortal-grade Divine Weapon.
However, with these runes, you will instead be forging an Immortal-grade Soul Weapon, one capable of housing a weapon spirit and continuing to grow stronger as time passes."
"But... but why would you do all this for me?
I only needed your Ice element."
Kent laughed, poured himself a drink, and took a sip.
"Let’s just say I’m impressed by your idea.
As someone who always wishes to see the very best in everything, I want you to have this opportunity to show the universe what you can do.
Who knows, maybe the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith would notice your efforts and take you as his disciple."
Of course, Kent wasn’t doing this out of the goodness of his heart.
He needed this weapon to finally lure his stubborn hammer back to his side.

chapters.title: Chapter 1760: The Ambush
paragraphs: Lady Khronisia stared long and intently at Kent before asking, "Is the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith really alive?"

She wasn’t asking because she wished to become his disciple. It was because she, like every blacksmith in existence, had heard about his legendary feats, and so many took him as their idol, herself included.
Of course, if she got to become the disciple of such a person who hadn’t been seen since the end of the Flame Era, she would be the happiest person in existence.

Kent smiled and answered, "I can tell you for a fact that the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith is still alive. So put in some effort, and who knows? He might just pop up and take you as his disciple. Just so you know, he has never taken a disciple before, but you might just become the first."
Lady Khronisia smiled and nodded. "While this would never happen, rest assured, I will do my best not to disappoint you. And thank you very much for accepting my request."
"No need to thank me. It has always been my dream to witness a true master at work, so I see this as an opportunity rather than an obligation."
His handsome smile calmed Lady Khronisia’s racing heartbeat. For the last five days, she had been waiting intently, wondering if Kent would really come to see her.
After all, he had just offended some very powerful people, so going into hiding was the best thing he could do in such a situation.
However, now that he was here, he had even made her a deal that far surpassed what she had asked for, making her very happy.
"How about this? I will travel with you to the Blacksmith Association so we can iron out some details while on the way. You can also show me around the association."
Lady Khronisia had no issues with this arrangement. It would give her the chance to learn more about Kent and, if possible, form a connection with him.
Unbeknownst to her, Kent had his own motives for doing this.
When he recovered Fjorge’s memories, he sensed a powerful yet familiar gaze land on him from far away. It was only for a moment, but he felt it and sensed the unruliness within those eyes.
He, of course, realized who it was, but despite wishing for his hammer to return to his side, the unruly bastard ignored him.
Kent knew he was playing hard to get, so he wanted to use Lady Khronisia’s craftsmanship to tell his hammer that, with or without him, he still is the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith.
He had lived with his hammer since he was seven years old, so he knew it best and knew it would come running regardless of how insignificant the craftsmanship was.
"First, let’s eat."
So they started to eat their fill, or rather, Kent ate his fill. He and food were inseparable after all, especially now that he had some aspect of the Barbarian bloodline flowing through him.

A while later, they departed on Lady Khronisia’s private ship. As someone from the Blacksmith Association, she wasn’t about to stand in line and wait for her turn to board public transport, which moved much more slowly and was very high-risk.
Her own ship was under her control, so she could travel at any pace she wanted.
Kent had already received a quest stating that Lady Khronisia would be attacked on her way back to the Blacksmith Association and that he had to save her.

He had no idea who would attack her or why, but the rewards that came with the quest were just too good to pass up. So, using the excuse of wanting to see the Blacksmith Association, he started traveling with her.
And as expected, ten hours into the journey, a powerful flame attack came from the void, heading straight for the ship—or at least it came close.
Kent, who had been on high alert, activated the Chaos Scale Shield around the ship the moment he sensed the attack.
The beam struck the shield, and a devastating explosion rocked the space channel, sending the ship hurtling into space.
Immediately, a team of fifteen Demigods surrounded the ship, their auras sealing the space around it.
Lady Khronisia, who had never anticipated an attack, grew tense as she saw these people. However, she immediately recognized them, causing her face to turn pale.
"Soul Temple agents," Kent muttered, his eyes narrowing at the fifteen Demigods, each reeking of either an extreme soul aura or a blood aura.

The Soul Temple is known for its dark arts. They use methods that others had frowned upon to gain power. To them, the lives of both the guilty and the innocent are merely nourishment for their growth.
So Kent hates them, and so do most people in the universe.

"This is the end of the line for you, Lady Khronisia. Hand over the Grand Mage Staff Blueprint and surrender to the Soul Temple, and your life will be spared. Resist, and we will kill you and use your body to nourish our strength."
One of them shouted, causing Lady Khronisia to tremble...
"Relax, I will take care of them," Kent said, tapping her on the shoulder. Then he moved forward, shielding her...
"It is quite heartbreaking to see a bunch of humans turn into animals." Kent shook his head. "Very sad, really."
"Who are you?" one of them asked, pointing his weapon at Kent, his aura overflowing...

"Me? I am just an ordinary boy who likes to get into trouble when he should just run." Kent laughed, then his eyes narrowed. "Also, I promised a dear friend of mine years ago that I would bring the Soul Temple to its knees, so you can say I am the bane of your existence."
"Hahahahahahah..."
They burst out laughing uncontrollably. However, to their shock, Kent also joined them in the laughter, causing all fifteen of them to narrow their eyes.
The next second, their eyes widened, horror appearing on their faces.
"This..."

All of them grew pale when, suddenly, they found themselves surrounded by a sea of swords. Kent decided to go all out from the start, so he unleashed the full power of the Sword Realm, and just as he had envisioned, every last one of them became stunned.
Then they all despaired, and before long, the horror on their faces became unmistakable.
"So long, losers."
Kent snapped his fingers, and the sea moved, consuming them whole. Their screams were swallowed, and their bodies, down to the last chunk of bone, were ground into meat paste and pure energy.
In less than five seconds, all fifteen Demigods died, and their souls appeared inside the Soul Universe, where Kenna, Bello, and Calix shared them among themselves and started to absorb them.
The ding sounded in his mind, signaling to Kent that he had completed the quest successfully.
Kent turned back to Lady Khronisia, who looked both pale and stunned.
"It is over now, so we can leave."
She nodded, and a few minutes later, they were back inside the space channel, traveling several miles per second.
Meanwhile, far away on a dark planet, a man growled and opened his eyes, sweat forming on his forehead...
He looked very angry, and for a short moment, a faint killing intent flashed across his face, "So you’ve returned huh, Genesis."

chapters.title: Chapter 1761: Blood Ancestor
paragraphs: Coming close to certain death left Lady Khronisia rattled.
She had no idea that the blueprint of a weapon he had never planned to craft just yet could cause her to nearly lose her life, had it not been for Kent saving her.
Just like most alchemists and blacksmiths, she wasn’t that skilled in combat. So while she might be a Demigod like the fifteen Soul Temple Agents, she wouldn’t have lasted a second against them.
And all this for what? Over something she had no use for...

"I can’t help but ask, why do you have the blueprint for the Grand Mage Staff? If I recall history correctly, the Grand Mage Staff was a weapon wielded by the Grand Arcane Heavenly Mage, Rohan of the Heavenly Dark Temple, during the Primordial Era."
Lady Khronisia didn’t seem stunned that Kent knew the origin of the blueprint. After all, she had seen how knowledgeable he was during the auction and the few times she had spent with him.

"It was given to me by my father, who got it from his father, and his father’s father. You can say it is a family heirloom since, from what my father told me, a blacksmith who was the originator of my bloodline was the one who crafted the Grand Mage Staff."
’Oh, so you are from Kallixtos’ bloodline, huh?’
As someone who had lived during the Primordial Era, he knew quite a lot, and one of them was the greatest blacksmith to ever live during the Primordial Era, the Golden Hammer Blacksmith, Kallixtos.
He and Chaos had been friends since he had commissioned a weapon from him before and had personally aided him with his flames in crafting a few others.
’I guess I now understand why the heavens wanted me to save her. It turns out she is from that old monster’s bloodline.’
Kent smiled and nodded. "Better hold on to it well, then. I have a feeling you will craft it sooner rather than later."

She only gave Kent a nod but said nothing else. She was still in deep shock, so she needed some time to process her emotions. In fact, now that she had escaped the first assassination attempt, she couldn’t help but wonder if it would be the last.

She even went further, wondering what would happen next when Kent wasn’t there to save her. If only she knew she had over ten shadow fiends hidden within her shadows, ready to go into battle at a moment’s notice.
"Kent Madson, I want—" Just before her words could fully leave her mouth, Kent pushed her hard, and the next second, she crashed into a chair inside a very stunning garden.
Outside, a sword arc cut through the ship and blasted it apart, sending Kent flying out of the universe channel, his body hurtling through space like a falling asteroid.
Inside the mountain garden, Pandora and her sisters appeared before Lady Khronisia, who was still in shock.
Before any of them could question her, Kent’s voice entered their minds, causing their bodies to freeze.
"Ladies, I am under attack from a Primordial. I will be fine, so none of you should come after me, especially not now. I will reach out if I need help. The lady there is call Khronisia"
"We have to go save him," Yukiko said, ready to teleport to where Kent was. However, Pandora stopped her.
"No. If he doesn’t want us to come, then it means he doesn’t want us to get hurt... even me. So let’s stay put and wait for him to reach back."
Pandora, who was also a Primordial, knew just how powerful someone like her truly was, so since Kent had asked them to stay put, they would.
Her sisters hated the idea, but as the strongest among them, they had to listen to her.
"Damn it."

Meanwhile, after flying for a while, Kent finally managed to stabilize his body. Just then, the void exploded open, and instead of a dark maw, a crimson one oozing with blood and the screams of resentful souls tore itself open.

From within, a man with metallic blue skin and three horns, one protruding directly from the center of his brow, stepped out. His deep black hair hung behind him, and his entire body looked as though it had been forged inside a furnace.
He appeared to be in his late sixties...
He wasn’t particularly handsome, but he was terrifying, and his crimson eyes held so much danger that the moment they met Kent’s, he felt as though his soul were being devoured from his body.
But Kent also recognized the man.
"It’s been a while, Genesis. Or do you prefer I call you the Slave Swordsman, Jest?" the man said, a sneer forming on his face.
Kent frowned and muttered coldly,
"Blood Ancestor..."
The man grinned.
"Why? Do you miss me?"
"Can’t say I have missed you. After all, I only miss beautiful things, and you blue-faced snotty-nose bastard is as ugly as they come. So no, I didn’t miss you even for a moment."
"Hahahaha!" Blood Ancestor laughed. "You know, considering how weak you are now and how overpowered I have become, it would be in your best interest to be on your best behavior, Genesis."
Kent spat out a mouthful of blood and straightened his back.
"So what? Are you such a sore loser that you couldn’t even wait for me to become a God before attacking me? Are you really that much of a loser, Gehan?"
During the Divine Era, Lord Genesis had offended many people, but only a few had come close to killing him. One of them was the Blood Ancestor, a high-ranking member of the Soul Temple.

Their conflict had started when Jest killed one of his disciples. However, after countless battles, it became clear who would win if they fought to the death. Jest failed to kill him simply because, whenever he did, the bastard always seemed to come back from the dead to haunt him again.
It was one of the reasons Kent didn’t want his wives to come to his aid. Even if they succeeded in killing him, he would simply return later, perhaps with even greater vengeance.

"You can’t blame me, Genesis. I have died 213 times by your sword, so I know that if anyone can truly kill me, it would be you. As the bane of my existence, it only makes sense for me to kill you first."
He extended his hand, and a blood mist condensed into a crimson sword.
"You can only blame yourself for using your Sword Realm this close to where I left one of my markers."
"Haaa..." Kent smiled and shook his head slightly. "Looks like I am at a crossroads here."
He sighed before looking directly into Gehan’s eyes.
"Your appearance wasn’t one I saw coming. However, I am not someone you can kill so easily, Gehan."
"Is that so?" Blood Ancestor smiled. "Tell me, how can you possibly escape with your Immortal Monarch strength? Even with your wings, you cannot run fast enough from me."
Kent merely smiled and narrowed his eyes at Blood Ancestor.
"You win today, Gehan. Next time, I will make sure you die only once... and in the most painful way possible."
Kent’s hand moved.
Before Blood Ancestor could even blink, Kent dug out his Chaos Heart and clenched it, shattering it.

Blood Ancestor’s eyes narrowed as he instantly moved. However, despite his overwhelming strength and speed, the resulting shockwave from the chaos heart explosion blasted him backward, while Kent was pulled away into a portal that closed behind him in an instant.
Inside the tower, a powerful wave of blood qi erupted from the thirteen moons in the sky before they all dimmed, leaving Kent’s wives deathly pale.
Their connection with Kent had been severed.

chapters.title: Chapter 1762: Chaos Chasm
paragraphs: "What just happened?" Vexthra asked, her expression pale as she stared at the thirteen moons in the sky. They used to be brighter, but now they seem rather pale and dim.
The rest of her sisters wore the same look, the same question on their minds. Just now, their connection to Kent was severed.
"Kent...he," Elina muttered, but before she could add the rest of her statement, Pandora stopped her.
"He is fine."
Her sisters turned to look at her, silently asking for more context.

"You all told me Kent is connected to the Tower at the soul level, and because of that, we can also connect with the Tower and with each other. Just now, when the connection with him was severed, we only felt our own connection severed for a moment before it was restored.
"This means he is still alive, and the Tower is still intact. It may be that wherever he is, the laws are preventing us from reaching him, making it appear as though he is dead.
"If he were truly dead, the Tower wouldn’t still be intact, and all of us would have been ejected by now."

"Lady Pandora is right. Master is still alive," Tower suddenly appeared in her small, angelic form, reassuring the ladies. "I don’t know where he is right now, but I can still feel my connection to him. His soul is still empowering me"
The ladies finally sighed in relief. However, Vexthra, who at that moment was close to reverting to her Divinity, which would have unleashed her Hatred and Resentment, asked, "What caused this?"
Tower simply waved her hand, and a projection of the Blood Ancestor appeared.
"Master called him the Blood Ancestor. He is a member of the Soul Temple and one of Master’s enemies from the Divine Era. He is a Primordial, and according to Master, he is unkillable."
"For now," Pandora said, her eyes narrowing.
"Master said you all should stay put. He doesn’t want any of you going after this person, so for now, we can only wait for him to return."
Tower had personally sensed the power within the Blood Ancestor, so she knew exactly what kind of monster he was. She didn’t want her master’s wives putting themselves in danger while he was away.
Suddenly, portals opened, and over four hundred shadow fiends appeared inside the Garden alongside Kent’s three Soul Warriors.
Seeing their master’s wives worried, they all sighed and joined them. They would have to obey their master’s orders and stay put for now. Once he returned, they would decide what to do next.
Meanwhile, back in space, where debris from the ship still drifted, the Blood Ancestor, whose real name was Gehan, looked stunned, his grip on his blood sword tightening.
"Damn it. He escaped," he gritted his teeth, shocked that even after becoming a Primordial four eras ago, he had failed to stop a mere Immortal from escaping his grasp.
He could tell Kent had sacrificed a lot to escape, but even so, he felt defeated that he had managed to slip away from him. That was simply too insulting.
"I will get my hands on you one day, Genesis. Just you wait. I will find you eventually."
He gritted his teeth once more before opening his special void portal and vanishing into it, the portal closing behind him.

A few minutes after he left, a figure clad in plain clothes and holding a folding fan appeared like a ghost. The person carried no aura whatsoever, nor did they use the void to move. However, a single glance was enough to tell that he possessed unfathomable power.
He waved his fan, and instantly, as though time itself had reversed, projections of the events from when Kent was blasted out of the space channel appeared before him.
The man calmly watched every scene unfold, all the way to the final moment, when Kent dug out his Chaos Heart and shattered it, creating an overwhelming shockwave and opening a portal.
He paused when the portal appeared and enlarged the projection.
"A Chaos Portal..." he murmured. "So he is back, huh?"

A smile formed on his face, but when the scene showed Kent vanishing into the Chaos Portal, a frown replaced it. He pressed his index finger against his forehead, and his eyes emitted a faint brown glow.
For a moment, his consciousness spread across nearly half the universe, yet he found nothing.
"Strange. Usually, the Chaos Portal takes him somewhere safe within this universe. So why isn’t he here?" he muttered.
He continued searching for a while longer, but when nothing turned up, he let out a sigh and stopped.
"He’ll be fine," he murmured before vanishing just as silently as he had appeared.
If Kent had been there to see this man, his eyes would have widened in shock.
During the Primordial Era, when he had grown fed up with how the clans on Planet Lumen were treating the people, he chose to venture into the Abyss to train and become strong enough to oppose them.
It was there that he met the man he came to know as Leviathan.

Leviathan was the one who had set Chaos upon the path that eventually led him to become the Primordial Chaos Dragon. Years later, after Kent had reached the pinnacle of his strength, Leviathan visited him once more, this time to bid him farewell.
He had planned to venture into the Primordial Chaos to see if he could ascend beyond the limits of his current power.
That was the last time they met.
Now, it seemed he had finally returned after spending who knows how long there, searching for his old friend and perhaps his unofficial disciple.
Unfortunately, he had arrived a few minutes too late.
Kent slowly opened his eyes, his entire body aching as though he had been struck by a speeding truck.
The first thing he saw, when his vision had barely cleared, was a system message floating before him.
[Your Chaos Heart has been destroyed.]
He swiped the message away before slowly pushing himself into a sitting position. His entire body still throbbed with pain, and his face was deathly pale.
"That was close," he muttered, his mind drifting back to his encounter with the Blood Ancestor.
He had come within a hair’s breadth of death.
Frankly, he knew his chances of escaping had been no more than two percent, yet he had still chosen to gamble.
If he had summoned Pandora, things could have ended disastrously, but also differently.
Although Pandora was unimaginably powerful, the Blood Ancestor exuded a level of danger that surpassed even hers.
He wouldn’t have needed to shatter his Chaos Heart had Pandora come to rescue him, but doing so would have forced his wife to stake her own life on the line.
That was something he had no intention of allowing.
"Well... she’d be furious if she found out I’ve underestimated her," he said with a faint smile.
He then inspected his body.
When his gaze landed on the gaping hole in his chest, he let out a weary sigh.
Gathering his energy, he attempted to heal the wound.
The very next second, however, his eyes flew open.
"Huh? What happened to my cores?"
His eyes widened even further when he realized he could no longer sense them.
His two Flame Cores, two Blood Cores, and Evil Core all seemed to have been sealed away.
Even more alarming, his Chaos Heart was truly gone.
He had shattered it just as Chaos had done during the Primordial Era to escape from enemies, which ultimately led him to the forsaken seer.
The difference was that Chaos had possessed three Chaos Hearts when he destroyed one. Destroying one had still left him with two others.
Kent, however, only possessed a single Chaos Heart.
Now that it was gone and his remaining cores had somehow been sealed, an overwhelming sense of danger washed over him.
"Tower... are you there?" Kent called.
No response came.
An even colder realization struck him.
He was sitting inside a completely sealed room where not even a breath of air could enter.
Suddenly, messages appeared before him...
<Requirements to awaken the Chaos Tower have been met.>
<Chaos tower is awakening>
<You have awakened the Chaos Tower: Tier 1>
<Welcome to Chaos Chasm, Primordial Chaos Dragon>

chapters.title: Chapter 1763: Chaos Tower
paragraphs: Kent blinked a few times, staring at the messages hovering before his eyes.

For a moment, he thought he was dreaming. However, that turned out to be false, as he could still feel the pain of losing his Chaos Heart. The hole in his chest is still there, and most importantly, he still cannot feel his other cores.
This meant he wasn’t dreaming, and the messages were indeed real.
’But how? What happened to Tower?’ he asked inwardly.
The next moment, a response appeared, causing his eyes to widen.

<I am Tower, but a different version of it. My role is explicitly tied to your Primordial Chaos Bloodline, and so now that you are only required to use Chaos Qi, I have awakened. My other version is still alive and will merge back with me when you leave this place, Master.>
’Oh, so that is how it works, huh? I suppose that can be managed. After all, Tower is Tier 3 while you are only Tier 1.’
Kent sighed in relief, knowing that with Tower around, he had nothing to fear.
While she couldn’t help him as she could back when she was Tier 3, he knew that with her around, things wouldn’t become too boring.
"Tower, tell me where I am and explain my condition in a clear and more vivid way. Basically, I want to know how screwed I am since I can’t feel any of my cores."
<The Master is indeed screwed, but this place is also a goldmine.
First of all, you are in a realm called the Chaos Chasm, a place where only beings with the ability to cultivate Chaos Qi can live. Everything in this world contains Chaos Essence.
However, since the Master has no Chaos Heart at the moment, aside from the natural Chaos Qi in the air, the Master cannot cultivate, absorb, or store it.
The Master can only form a new Chaos Heart and then cultivate from there. Thankfully, the Master has an unusually powerful bloodline, so forming a new Chaos Heart will be a breeze.
With the natural Chaos Qi in the air, the Master can consume the Chaos Stones in his possession and form a new Chaos Heart.>
"That is a bit convenient. But how screwed am I?"

<The Master appears to be in some form of prison. This suggests that while you were unconscious, someone took custody of your body and imprisoned you here. Until we find out who, the Master can only stay put.>
"Then can you contact my wives and tell them I am okay?" Kent asked, clearly worried that his wives would go after the Blood Ancestor. If they did, there would be a disaster he couldn’t even imagine.

<I cannot contact them, Master. However, based on the conversation you had with the other version of me before entering the Chaos Portal, I am sure the other version of me will do everything possible to keep them from going after your enemy.>
Kent sighed in relief.
The last thing he wanted was for his wives to get into trouble because of him. They were too precious for him to take for granted.
Thankfully, he knew Tower was right. He had told them to stay put and had even instructed Tower to keep them safe, since he knew she could exist in multiple places at once.
Now, he could focus on himself.
"Tower, how fast can I form the Chaos Heart, and what resources do you have for me?"

<The Master currently has three Chaos Stones, one Green Essence Chaos Fruit, and the Black Flame Chaos Flower. They were left inside your Soul Sea by the other me. So by calculation, you need less than 5 days>
Kent smiled, knowing Tower always went above and beyond for him.
She had anticipated that he would be in danger, so she had made a decision—one that would now save his life.
"Talk about the Soul Sea. What else remains useful there? Without my Chaos Heart, I cannot access it, so tell me, Tower."

<The Master’s Soul Sea is still intact. However, until the Master forms a Chaos Heart, the Master cannot access it or summon his weapons. Most importantly, until the Master forms a new Chaos Heart, he cannot make use of Lady Kenzie, who has been sealed alongside the other cores.>
That explained everything to Kent.
He had wondered why he was still injured, given that Lady Kenzie was basically his overpowered healer.

Even when he fought Meiko, the injuries he sustained should have taken a week to heal. However, with Lady Kenzie’s overwhelming healing abilities, she had used Meiko’s energy to heal him in mere minutes.
"Before forming the Chaos Heart, can you tell me how I can get out of here, this realm I mean?" Kent asked, but Tower’s response was discouraging.
<Unfortunately, I have no idea how the Master can return. However, that will change once the Master is out of this prison. For now, let’s get the Master back into shape.>
Kent smiled and nodded.
He sat down in a lotus position and closed his eyes.
A few seconds later, he opened them again, grabbed one of the five items hovering before him, and swallowed it.
A few seconds later, he swallowed the second, then the third, fourth, and finally the fifth before closing his eyes once more.
Moments later, waves of Chaos Qi began to pour out of his body, filling the room.

Kent had already formed a Chaos Heart once before, so he had already endured the unbearable pain that accompanied its creation. As a result, the reformation process progressed smoothly without him feeling any discomfort.
In no time, the foundation of the Chaos Heart began to take shape.

Meanwhile, inside a massive hall where humanoids, each easily over three meters tall, sat on enormous chairs, their expressions were filled with intrigue and shock as they watched Kent through a projection.
Most of them possessed horns, while a few had metallic skin and heavily muscular arms and legs.
Only two of them were much shorter—that is, if two meters could even be considered short—and far more human-looking than the others.
Surprisingly, the pair, a man and a woman, also happened to be the strongest, judging by the overwhelming aura radiating from them.
"Interesting. I never thought the day would come when I would witness someone form a Chaos Heart by themselves," the woman muttered, a smile spreading across her face.
The others around her smiled as well.
"Where did you find him again?" she asked, turning to one of the giants with purple metallic skin and a muscular physique powerful enough to crush even a Peak Celestial with a single punch.

"I found him near the border. He fell out of a portal that looked eerily similar to the one described in the history books. At first, I thought he was dead, but when I got closer, I sensed an unusually refined aura coming from him. So I brought him back for you to decide what to do with him.
If he proves useful, we can recruit him for that mission. If he turns out to be trash, throwing him out won’t be a problem," the man said...
"Well, you can remove ’throwing him out’ from our plans. Someone capable of forming a Chaos Heart by themselves is perhaps the talent we need right now.
Let’s wait until he is finished. Then we can question him and see whether he is willing to join us. If not, we can send him to that place, where death is certain."

chapters.title: Chapter 1764: Chaos Heart Formed
paragraphs: <Congratulations. You have formed your first Chaos Heart.>
<You can now absorb and store Chaos Qi. Current Saturation: 20%.>
<You can now access your Soul Sea and make use of your other cores’ essence.>
Kent opened his eyes and smiled, feeling his strength return to how it was before he dug out his Chaos Heart.
For a moment, he had thought he was finished. After all, losing access to all his energy and his Soul Sea was hardly a cause for celebration.

However, he had managed to form a new Chaos Heart, restoring everything. While replenishing his other cores would now require absorbing Chaos Qi and converting it into the appropriate energies, he could once again make use of every core under his command.
Without hesitation, Kent sent his consciousness into his Soul Sea, arriving beside the cocoon that housed Lady Kenzie.
He gently tapped it, and the cocoon unraveled, revealing the flawless beauty who had been serving as his Soul Guardian for the last couple of months.
The moment she was freed, she formed a hand seal, causing the wound on Kent’s soul to heal instantly.
The sudden recovery caused the people watching from the hall to furrow their brows.
Their interest in Kent increased yet again.
"What happened, my lord? One moment I was healing you, and the next, I was sealed away," Lady Kenzie asked after healing Kent.
"We are outside the universe... or perhaps still within it, but inside a realm detached from it. It is a place called the Chaos Chasm."
"Chaos Chasm? I have never heard of such a place before," she replied, clearly puzzled. Despite having lived for millions of years, she had never encountered such a name.
"Neither have I. However, we’re here now, so we’ll be getting some answers soon."
She nodded. After ensuring that every injury, both inside and outside Kent’s body, had completely healed, she let out a soft sigh before asking,
"What is the next plan, Master?"
"I am currently being held in a prison, so let’s wait for the people who imprisoned me to make contact. For now, simply observe. If danger arises, do your best to keep me alive."
"I will, Master," she replied.
Kent nodded before withdrawing his consciousness from the Soul Sea.
’What now, Tower?’ Kent asked after returning to his body.

<The Master has now formed a Chaos Heart. With the abundance of Chaos Essence in the air, I advise the Master to saturate the heart as much as possible. Later, we will figure out how to form the second Chaos Heart.
I have a feeling that if we play our cards right, the Master will leave this place far more powerful than you are now.>
’If I can leave, that is,’ Kent thought with a faint smile before closing his eyes once more and beginning to absorb the Chaos Essence that permeated the air.
Naturally, Kent was taken aback when waves of Chaos Essence, far purer than what he had absorbed in the Tormented Chaos Abyss, began rushing into his Chaos Heart.
In fact, compared to that place, the Chaos Essence here was on an entirely different level.
In no time, his Chaos Heart began filling with an astonishing amount of Chaos Essence. Even Kent was dumbfounded by the sheer quantity he was absorbing.
’This place is a paradise for Chaos energy cultivators,’ he thought with a smile before continuing to absorb it. The more he absorbed, the stronger he became.
Twenty-four hours later, Kent had absorbed enough Chaos Essence into his Chaos Heart with only fifteen percent away from full saturation.
However, he was forced to stop when the walls around him began to move.
Soon, an opening appeared to his left, causing Kent to become alert and quickly rise to his feet. He already knew what was about to happen, so he walked out before anyone even asked him to.
In no time, he found himself outside, gazing at a gray sky.
Even more astonishing, the Chaos Essence in the air was at least ten times denser than it had been inside the prison.
’This is just incredible,’ he thought inwardly.
However, his expression quickly changed when he sensed three presences behind him.
Turning sharply, his eyes landed on three towering figures, each standing well over ten feet tall, their mere presence radiating overwhelming authority.
"This..." Kent instinctively stumbled back several meters as beads of sweat formed on his forehead the moment he sensed the terrifying aura surrounding them.
"Primordials..."
"That would be Primordial Gods, little dragon," one of them corrected.

He crouched down slightly, lowering his enormous frame enough to speak to Kent face-to-face. Even though Kent stood at seven feet three inches in his demi-dragon form, he still looked like an insect before the giant.
"My name is Kwame, leader of the City Guards and the one who brought you here."
He gestured toward the woman standing beside him, whose towering and imposing figure commanded equal respect and power.
"She is Mrinali, and he is Devak, my immediate subordinate."
"Welcome to the Red Bone Chaos Tribe," Mrinali said with a small wave.
Despite possessing the bloodline of the Primordial Chaos Dragon, Kent couldn’t help but feel suffocated by the overwhelming pressure emanating from the three.
Forget the Blood Ancestor. Just one casual slap from any of these Primordial Gods, and not even a fragment of his bones would remain.
"May we know your name?" Kwame asked.
Kent, still shaken to his core, forced himself to answer.
"My name is Kent Madson."
"Kent Madson... I can’t say I recognize that name," Kwame muttered thoughtfully.
Mrinali and Devak wore similar expressions.
"Are you from the Black Flame Chaos Dragon Tribe?" Kwame asked.
A faint strand of killing intent leaked from his body, and Kent immediately caught it.
He knew he absolutely could not answer yes—even if it were true.
"No. I am from a place called the Infinity Universe."
"Huh... You’re a Traveler."
The three Primordial Gods visibly trembled with excitement.
Before Kent could react, the world around him blurred.
The next instant, he found himself standing inside a vast hall, facing a much smaller humanoid whose aura he couldn’t perceive at all.
That alone told Kent everything he needed to know.
She was far stronger than the three Primordial Gods.
The realization left him so shocked that he completely failed to notice everyone else gathered inside the hall.
"You said you are from the Infinity Universe," the woman said. "Do you, by any chance, have any connection to the Chaos Ascension King?"

She possessed long flowing brown hair and a lean yet muscular physique befitting a seasoned warrior. Although she was seated, Kent could tell she was around eight feet tall. She wore leather-like armor woven from an incredibly durable material.
"I am from the Infinity Universe," Kent replied, "but I don’t know, nor have I ever heard of, the person you mentioned. In fact, this is my first time hearing that name."
"I see."
She nodded thoughtfully.

"Then can you tell me how you arrived here? In the past, every Traveler who came here was summoned by one of the Seven Tribes to challenge the Chaos Ascension Tower. You are the first to arrive here on your own, and within the territory of our Red Bone Chaos Tribe.
"If this had happened anywhere else, I would have assumed someone had summoned you. But none of us did, so tell me, Kent Madson... how did you get here?"
Kent let out a slow sigh before answering.

"I dug out my Chaos Heart and shattered it. Then, I used the power produced to open a Chaos Portal. I was supposed to be teleported somewhere far away from the place where my Chaos Heart was destroyed.
"But for reasons I still don’t understand, I ended up here instead."
He paused briefly before continuing.
"I was actually hoping these seniors could tell me whether there is a way back to my universe... and if so, how I can return."

sentences.text: <Congratulations.
You have formed your first Chaos Heart.>
<You can now absorb and store Chaos Qi.
Current Saturation: 20%.>
<You can now access your Soul Sea and make use of your other cores’ essence.>
Kent opened his eyes and smiled, feeling his strength return to how it was before he dug out his Chaos Heart.
For a moment, he had thought he was finished.
After all, losing access to all his energy and his Soul Sea was hardly a cause for celebration.
However, he had managed to form a new Chaos Heart, restoring everything.
While replenishing his other cores would now require absorbing Chaos Qi and converting it into the appropriate energies, he could once again make use of every core under his command.
Without hesitation, Kent sent his consciousness into his Soul Sea, arriving beside the cocoon that housed Lady Kenzie.
He gently tapped it, and the cocoon unraveled, revealing the flawless beauty who had been serving as his Soul Guardian for the last couple of months.
The moment she was freed, she formed a hand seal, causing the wound on Kent’s soul to heal instantly.
The sudden recovery caused the people watching from the hall to furrow their brows.
Their interest in Kent increased yet again.
"What happened, my lord?
One moment I was healing you, and the next, I was sealed away," Lady Kenzie asked after healing Kent.
"We are outside the universe... or perhaps still within it, but inside a realm detached from it.
It is a place called the Chaos Chasm."
"Chaos Chasm?
I have never heard of such a place before," she replied, clearly puzzled.
Despite having lived for millions of years, she had never encountered such a name.
"Neither have I.
However, we’re here now, so we’ll be getting some answers soon."
She nodded.
After ensuring that every injury, both inside and outside Kent’s body, had completely healed, she let out a soft sigh before asking,
"What is the next plan, Master?"

For now, simply observe.
If danger arises, do your best to keep me alive."
"I will, Master," she replied.

<The Master has now formed a Chaos Heart.
With the abundance of Chaos Essence in the air, I advise the Master to saturate the heart as much as possible.
Later, we will figure out how to form the second Chaos Heart.
I have a feeling that if we play our cards right, the Master will leave this place far more powerful than you are now.>

Even Kent was dumbfounded by the sheer quantity he was absorbing.
’This place is a paradise for Chaos energy cultivators,’ he thought with a smile before continuing to absorb it.
The more he absorbed, the stronger he became.
Twenty-four hours later, Kent had absorbed enough Chaos Essence into his Chaos Heart with only fifteen percent away from full saturation.

Turning sharply, his eyes landed on three towering figures, each standing well over ten feet tall, their mere presence radiating overwhelming authority.
"This..." Kent instinctively stumbled back several meters as beads of sweat formed on his forehead the moment he sensed the terrifying aura surrounding them.
"Primordials..."
"That would be Primordial Gods, little dragon," one of them corrected.
He crouched down slightly, lowering his enormous frame enough to speak to Kent face-to-face.
Even though Kent stood at seven feet three inches in his demi-dragon form, he still looked like an insect before the giant.
"My name is Kwame, leader of the City Guards and the one who brought you here."
He gestured toward the woman standing beside him, whose towering and imposing figure commanded equal respect and power.
"She is Mrinali, and he is Devak, my immediate subordinate."
"Welcome to the Red Bone Chaos Tribe," Mrinali said with a small wave.

Forget the Blood Ancestor.
Just one casual slap from any of these Primordial Gods, and not even a fragment of his bones would remain.

Kent, still shaken to his core, forced himself to answer.
"My name is Kent Madson."
"Kent Madson...
I can’t say I recognize that name," Kwame muttered thoughtfully.
Mrinali and Devak wore similar expressions.

He knew he absolutely could not answer yes—even if it were true.
"No.
I am from a place called the Infinity Universe."
"Huh...
You’re a Traveler."
The three Primordial Gods visibly trembled with excitement.

The next instant, he found himself standing inside a vast hall, facing a much smaller humanoid whose aura he couldn’t perceive at all.

chapters.title: Chapter 1765: Chaos Ascension King
paragraphs: Kent knew asking for a way back home when he had just met these people was asking for too much. However, to his shock, his question was answered.
"There is a way out of this place. However, I am not sure you can handle it, especially with how fragile you are..." the lady responded, and the others laughed.
This made Kent finally sense their presence, causing him to frown a bit. Right now, there were 12 people in the hall, and 2 of them were far stronger than Kwame and the 2 he had seen outside.
In fact, the remaining ten were far stronger than the Blood Ancestor. This made him wonder just what they were capable of, or more importantly, how any of this was even possible.

From what he had learned about Primordials, they were the absolute beings of every universe. However, in every era, fewer than five were born. So it could be that, across all thirteen eras of the Infinity Universe, no more than a dozen Primordials had ever existed.
So having twelve of them gathered in a single room was clearly shocking.
’Just who are these people?’ he wondered inwardly. Then he sighed and asked the most important question.
"I still want to know. I am very important to many people, so staying here is not possible. I must return to my universe as soon as possible. So how can I go back."
The twelve people exchanged glances, and the lady sighed.
"Very well, I will tell you what you need to know. However, in return, you will share the method you used to form your Chaos Heart with us."

"Deal." Kent didn’t even bat an eye, showing he meant it when he said he wanted to go home. He knew the longer he remained separated from his wives, the more worried they would become, so he had to return home.
"Before I tell you how you can return to your universe, I must first tell you the history of the Chaos Ascension King, the absolute ruler of this world.
This world, called Chaos Chasm, has seven tribes, including the Red Bone Chaos Tribe.

A very long time ago, long before our ancestors were born, there existed a man known as the Universe King. None of us knew where he came from, or what he came here to do, but they said he was so powerful that a mere flick of his hand was all it would take to reduce an entire universe to dust.
Some parts of the history books say he came to this world to cultivate a powerful technique, others say he came to take a nap, while some say he came to create his own race.

But one thing was certain: whatever he came here to do, after succeeding, he created the seven tribes and bestowed upon each of them a unique cultivation art, with our Red Bone Chaos Tribe receiving the Red Bone Chaos Devouring Art.
Over the years, legendary warriors rose from within our ranks. However, as you can see, we are all that remains of the Red Bone Chaos Tribe."
"What happened to the others?" Kent asked, seeing how the conversation was unfolding.
"They ventured into the Primordial Chaos and never returned.
Before the Chaos Ascension King left, he told us that the only way we could leave this place was by passing his trial, known as the Chaos Ascension Tower Trial.

Over the years, many have attempted it, but none have succeeded. So if you want to leave this place, you must challenge the Chaos Ascension Tower and pass its trial. Failure means you will remain here with us forever."
Kent frowned slightly, not expecting things to be this serious.

In his mind, he had expected the way out of this place to involve asking the Chaos Ascension King for a favor. After all, he sounded like someone capable of anything. Instead, he now found himself facing a situation that didn’t require a genius to realize was extremely dangerous.

"Forget about it, little Human. Many of us have challenged the Chaos Ascension Tower and failed. You haven’t even stepped into divinity yet, so it’s not as though you can even enter and challenge it."
One of the tall Primordials said with a sigh.
"He is right, Kent Madson. Only Demigods and above are qualified to challenge the Chaos Ascension Tower. So you should forget about leaving this place for now and instead focus on growing stronger.
Perhaps one day, when you reach our level, you can try your luck," Kwame said, making Kent frown deeply.
"Unfortunately, I have no plans on staying here for long, so I will challenge it. As for becoming a Demigod, I just need to saturate my cores and, if possible, form more."
"Hold on a minute," the lady seated in the main chair exclaimed, causing Kent to narrow his eyes at her.
"Did you just say you can form more cores? You mean... more Chaos Hearts?"
Kent shook his head.

Yes. I only have one Chaos Heart. However, what I meant is that I can form other types of cores. The Chaos Heart is just one of them. While I don’t have a reliable way to replenish the other energies as I do with Chaos Essence, I can absorb Chaos Essence and convert it into those respective energies."
The lady stared at him for a long moment before speaking again.
"Curious... but can you tell me how many other cores you have?"

Kent sighed. Then he extended his hand, channeling his Blood Core, Flame Core, and Evil Core. Three spheres of crimson, blazing green, and sinister black energy condensed above his palm, each radiating an entirely different aura.
"Heavens..."
All twelve people inside the hall shot to their feet, their expressions frozen in disbelief.
"This is..." the lady muttered as she slowly walked toward Kent. "Are you sure you and the Chaos Ascension King aren’t related somehow?"
"I can assure you we aren’t related in any way." Kent shrugged. "But I have to ask... why do all of you look so shocked?"
The lady took a deep breath before answering.

"In the billions of years I have lived, the only person I have ever known to possess more than one core was the Chaos Ascension King himself. According to our ancient records, he possessed twelve different cores... and multiple copies of each."
Her gaze remained fixed on the three energy spheres floating above Kent’s palm.
"You may be connected to him in some way without even realizing it."
Kent laughed, but even for a moment, he couldn’t help but consider the notion.
"Well, if he and I are related, then perhaps he’ll beam me back to my universe at any moment now."
The people inside the hall burst into laughter.
"I suppose you’re right. Perhaps all of this is merely an extraordinary coincidence." The lady smiled before her expression turned serious once more.
"Even so, I refuse to believe your arrival here today is meaningless.
If you are willing, I would like to sponsor your cultivation. In return, you will represent my tribe in the upcoming Chaos Ascension King Trial."
Kent remained silent, allowing her to continue.

"None of the Seven Chaos Tribes knows what truly awaits at the end of the Chaos Ascension Tower, but we believe our freedom awaits us. Every 100,000 years, each tribe selects a representative to challenge it.
The next trial will begin fifty years from now.
If you agree, the Red Bone Chaos Tribe will provide you with every resource you require to increase your strength. When the trial begins, you will represent our tribe."
Kent blinked several times as a familiar translucent screen appeared before his eyes.
<You have received a contract offer from the leaders of the Red Bone Chaos Tribe.>
<Objective: Represent the Red Bone Chaos Tribe in the upcoming Chaos Ascension King Trial.>
<Reward: The Red Bone Chaos Tribe will provide any cultivation resources within their means to aid your growth over the next fifty years.>
<Do you wish to accept this contract?>
[Y/N]
’Fuck me sideways... isn’t this a gold mine?’

chapters.title: Chapter 1766 - 50 Years Of Cultivation (1)
paragraphs: <You have accepted the contract offered by the leaders of the Red Bone Chaos Tribe. Failure to live up to your end of the bargain will result in the detonation of all your Chaos Hearts formed between now and the 50 years ahead of you.>

"Hmm..." Kent smiled as he read the message after choosing to align himself with the Red Bone Chaos Tribe. He would be a clown not to accept such an offer when they weren’t asking him to win, but merely to represent them.
That meant that even if he failed the trial, they wouldn’t impose any penalty.

However, they had also sensed his desire to leave this place, so they offered him a chance to try his luck. Now, he knew he had no choice but to handle his end of the bargain, even if, during the 50-year period, he found a way to return to his universe.
He had more than enough time to handle everything else.
’This is a golden opportunity. I’d better not waste it.’
"Now that we have entered something akin to a contract, I will introduce myself..." the woman said, drawing Kent’s attention back to her.
"My name is Jyoti Lata. I am a True Eternal and the leader of the Red Bone Chaos Tribe."
Kent furrowed his brow upon hearing an unfamiliar term. "Hold on a minute, Lady Jyoti Lata. Is True Eternal the next cultivation stage after Primordial, or is it a title?"
When he had walked out of the prison, the giants he encountered had referred to themselves as Primordial Kings. At the time, he hadn’t paid much attention to it, assuming it was insignificant.
Now that Jyoti Lata had mentioned something entirely new, he couldn’t help but ask.
She smiled and replied, "It is the next stage, Kent Madson. The Primordial Stage may seem like the peak to you, but to us, it is merely the beginning."
"Can you elaborate further?" Kent asked, sensing that something monumental was about to be revealed.

"Why not?" She raised her right hand and held up a single finger. "In this world, every child is born a Demigod. By the age of five to ten, they become Gods. Then, before they turn fifteen, they are expected to become Supremes.

Most people become Celestials by the age of forty, sometimes even earlier, and by the time they reach one hundred, they should have entered the Early Primordial Stage. To us, that is when one comes of age, and it is also when true cultivation truly begins.
From there, one advances from Early Primordial to Real Primordial, then True Primordial. After that come King, Emperor, Monarch, Lord, and finally God, in that order.
Only after reaching that point does one step into the Eternal Realm. The stages are Early Eternal, Real Eternal, and True Eternal.
As for me..." she smiled faintly, "...I am currently at the True Eternal Stage."

Kent was left stunned, unsure how to process everything he had just heard. His mind simply refused to accept the fact that even a newborn baby in this world possessed a cultivation realm higher than his own.
"Just what kind of world is this... and why has no one in my universe ever heard of it?"
The people in the room laughed.
"This is a world where the rules were written by the Chaos Ascension King. Comparing it to your own is a great insult to our ruler."
"I apologize for that. It’s just that I never expected this world to have such a mind-bending cultivation system. It’s like I’m seeing everything for the very first time."
"It is only natural. To us, however, this is simply life."

"I can see that now. But aside from the Eternal Stage, are there other realms beyond it?" Kent asked. Even if she chose not to answer, he had already gained invaluable insight into what lay beyond the Primordial Stage.

"Above the Eternal Stage are the Universe King, Universe Lord, and Universe God realms. Each of these realms has nine minor stages known as Universe Tiers. For example, one can be a Tier 1 or Tier 9 Universe King.
"Here, once you reach the Tier 1 Universe King realm, you will be sent into the Primordial Chaos, as this world can no longer help you grow."
Kent took a deep breath and nodded. "Thank you for revealing this to me. I will do my best to cultivate harder and perform even better during the Chaos Ascension King Trial."
The others then introduced themselves, allowing Kent to better understand the group’s hierarchy. The two who appeared younger and much smaller compared to the giants were both Eternals.
However, Jyoti Lata was a True Eternal, while the other, Ragini Disha, was a Real Eternal, one stage below Jyoti Lata.
After the introductions, they asked Kent what he needed.

Kent, naturally, intended to make full use of this opportunity, so he listed over a thousand resources that would help him increase the number of cores and awaken the Third Blood Gate, allowing him to form his third Blood Core and subsequent ones.

He also planned to form his Ice Core, perhaps even more than one, along with his Lightning Core. In addition, he intended to create more Chaos Hearts and, most importantly, temper his body so it could withstand the burden of wielding multiple cores simultaneously in battle.

Lastly, he wanted to temper his Divine Sword Energy to its next realm—the Extreme Stage. His only hope was that by the time he returned, the Genesis Sword Dao Competition, which he needed to win to ascend to the realm of Sword Legend, would not have ended.
After all, he would be cultivating here for fifty years.
To Kent’s astonishment, after hearing his lengthy list of requests, Jyoti Lata simply replied, "Okay," and assured him that everything would be prepared within an hour.
She then casually added that if he needed anything else, he only had to ask, and someone would provide it.
For a brief moment, Kent wished he could return to this place whenever he wanted.
However, he knew there was no guarantee he would ever leave this world alive, so all he could do was focus on making the most of the opportunity before him.

That said, he also planned to bring back some of the world’s unique ores and minerals for blacksmithing. A world where Primordials were treated the same way Celestials were in the Infinity Universe was bound to possess extraordinary treasures.
An hour later, he was escorted to a cultivation ground where every single item he had requested had already been gathered. There were even numerous treasures he had never asked for.

"You may stay here for the duration of your cultivation. If you need anything, simply let us know, and we will provide it," Kwame, the Primordial God who had found him unconscious and brought him to the Red Bone Chaos Tribe, said after leading Kent into the vast training ground.
"Thank you, Senior. I’ll let you know if I need anything."
Kent walked inside. After spending an entire day organizing everything and devising a comprehensive cultivation plan, he finally began his secluded cultivation.
He planned to first form a second Chaos Heart, followed by an Ice Core and a Lightning Core. After that, he would move on to forming another Evil Core.

To his surprise, the Red Bone Chaos Tribe had actually managed to gather treasures overflowing with resentment and death energy. More importantly, they had provided over a hundred treasures that contained pure True Evil Qi.
With resources like these, Kent intended to forge even more cores.

Once he had filled the first two Blood Gates with the various elemental and special cores, if time still remained, he would awaken the Third Blood Gate and continue expanding his arsenal even further.
Time soon passed...

Now that Jyoti Lata had mentioned something entirely new, he couldn’t help but ask.
She smiled and replied, "It is the next stage, Kent Madson.
The Primordial Stage may seem like the peak to you, but to us, it is merely the beginning."
"Can you elaborate further?" Kent asked, sensing that something monumental was about to be revealed.
"Why not?" She raised her right hand and held up a single finger.
"In this world, every child is born a Demigod.
By the age of five to ten, they become Gods.
Then, before they turn fifteen, they are expected to become Supremes.
Most people become Celestials by the age of forty, sometimes even earlier, and by the time they reach one hundred, they should have entered the Early Primordial Stage.
To us, that is when one comes of age, and it is also when true cultivation truly begins.
From there, one advances from Early Primordial to Real Primordial, then True Primordial.
After that come King, Emperor, Monarch, Lord, and finally God, in that order.
Only after reaching that point does one step into the Eternal Realm.
The stages are Early Eternal, Real Eternal, and True Eternal.
As for me..." she smiled faintly, "...I am currently at the True Eternal Stage."
Kent was left stunned, unsure how to process everything he had just heard.
His mind simply refused to accept the fact that even a newborn baby in this world possessed a cultivation realm higher than his own.
"Just what kind of world is this... and why has no one in my universe ever heard of it?"
The people in the room laughed.
"This is a world where the rules were written by the Chaos Ascension King.
Comparing it to your own is a great insult to our ruler."
"I apologize for that.
It’s just that I never expected this world to have such a mind-bending cultivation system.
It’s like I’m seeing everything for the very first time."
"It is only natural.
To us, however, this is simply life."
"I can see that now.
But aside from the Eternal Stage, are there other realms beyond it?" Kent asked.
Even if she chose not to answer, he had already gained invaluable insight into what lay beyond the Primordial Stage.
"Above the Eternal Stage are the Universe King, Universe Lord, and Universe God realms.
Each of these realms has nine minor stages known as Universe Tiers.
For example, one can be a Tier 1 or Tier 9 Universe King.
"Here, once you reach the Tier 1 Universe King realm, you will be sent into the Primordial Chaos, as this world can no longer help you grow."
Kent took a deep breath and nodded.
"Thank you for revealing this to me.
I will do my best to cultivate harder and perform even better during the Chaos Ascension King Trial."
The others then introduced themselves, allowing Kent to better understand the group’s hierarchy.
The two who appeared younger and much smaller compared to the giants were both Eternals.
However, Jyoti Lata was a True Eternal, while the other, Ragini Disha, was a Real Eternal, one stage below Jyoti Lata.
After the introductions, they asked Kent what he needed.

Kent, naturally, intended to make full use of this opportunity, so he listed over a thousand resources that would help him increase the number of cores and awaken the Third Blood Gate, allowing him to form his third Blood Core and subsequent ones.
He also planned to form his Ice Core, perhaps even more than one, along with his Lightning Core.
In addition, he intended to create more Chaos Hearts and, most importantly, temper his body so it could withstand the burden of wielding multiple cores simultaneously in battle.
Lastly, he wanted to temper his Divine Sword Energy to its next realm—the Extreme Stage.
His only hope was that by the time he returned, the Genesis Sword Dao Competition, which he needed to win to ascend to the realm of Sword Legend, would not have ended.
After all, he would be cultivating here for fifty years.
To Kent’s astonishment, after hearing his lengthy list of requests, Jyoti Lata simply replied, "Okay," and assured him that everything would be prepared within an hour.
She then casually added that if he needed anything else, he only had to ask, and someone would provide it.
For a brief moment, Kent wished he could return to this place whenever he wanted.
However, he knew there was no guarantee he would ever leave this world alive, so all he could do was focus on making the most of the opportunity before him.
That said, he also planned to bring back some of the world’s unique ores and minerals for blacksmithing.
A world where Primordials were treated the same way Celestials were in the Infinity Universe was bound to possess extraordinary treasures.
An hour later, he was escorted to a cultivation ground where every single item he had requested had already been gathered.
There were even numerous treasures he had never asked for.
"You may stay here for the duration of your cultivation.

If you need anything, simply let us know, and we will provide it," Kwame, the Primordial God who had found him unconscious and brought him to the Red Bone Chaos Tribe, said after leading Kent into the vast training ground.
"Thank you, Senior.
I’ll let you know if I need anything."
Kent walked inside.
After spending an entire day organizing everything and devising a comprehensive cultivation plan, he finally began his secluded cultivation.
He planned to first form a second Chaos Heart, followed by an Ice Core and a Lightning Core.
After that, he would move on to forming another Evil Core.
To his surprise, the Red Bone Chaos Tribe had actually managed to gather treasures overflowing with resentment and death energy.
More importantly, they had provided over a hundred treasures that contained pure True Evil Qi.
With resources like these, Kent intended to forge even more cores.

Once he had filled the first two Blood Gates with the various elemental and special cores, if time still remained, he would awaken the Third Blood Gate and continue expanding his arsenal even further.
Time soon passed...

chapters.title: Chapter 1767 - 50 Years Of Cultivation (2)
paragraphs: <Congratulations, you have saturated your first Chaos Heart.>
Just a few minutes into his cultivation, Kent had completely saturated his first Chaos Heart.

His Evil Core, Flame Cores, and Blood Core were already more than halfway saturated, as he had only depleted a portion of their energy to fuel the Chaos Heart Detonation back in the Infinity Universe.
Now that his Chaos Heart had been fully restored, he turned his attention to saturating the rest of his cores.
Before forming his second Chaos Heart, Ice Core, and Lightning Core, he wanted every one of his existing cores to reach full saturation.
So he began cultivating once more, and the results soon became apparent.
<Congratulations, you have saturated your first Flame Core.>
<Congratulations, you have saturated your second Flame Core.>
<Congratulations, you have saturated your first Blood Core.>
<Congratulations, you have saturated your first Evil Core.>
’Damn... this feeling is incredible,’ he thought to himself as every one of his cores brimmed with overwhelming power.
The sensation of untamed energy coursing through his veins made him eager to discover how much stronger he would become once he forged his remaining cores.
Without hesitation, he decided to begin forming his Ice Core.

Using treasures provided by Primordials truly was a blessing. The moment he began refining the Ice Source, which had been compressed into a tiny bottle, Kent realized he might have underestimated just how precious the resources here were.
The Ice Source alone was sufficient to establish the core’s foundation.
Time quietly passed.
Before long, an entire month had gone by, yet his Ice Core was still taking shape. Kent, however, wasn’t in the slightest bit anxious. He still had fifty years ahead of him.
Time was on his side.
Three months later, a terrifying wave of frost erupted from his body, instantly freezing the surrounding space beneath a layer of crystalline ice.
Kent slowly opened his eyes, a smile spreading across his face as he realized another hurdle had been overcome.
<Congratulations, you have formed your first Ice Core.>
Kent smiled as he examined his body, feeling a majestic surge of ice essence flowing through every inch of his being.
"This feeling..."
He slowly clenched his fist, sensing his physical strength rise yet again.
Inside the First Blood Gate, the Blood Core still occupied the highest position, radiating an overwhelming wave of blood energy.
Beneath it floated the Green Flame Core, now overflowing with boundless flame essence.
The Chaos Heart hovered in the third position, followed closely by the Evil Core.
Now, a pure-white Ice Core rested in the fifth position, emanating an endless chill that seemed capable of freezing all creation.
The energy contained within his First Blood Gate alone was now sufficient to sustain prolonged battles without any fear of exhausting his power.
Thousands more Flame Runes had awakened during the process, while his Blood Runes had also become significantly potent.
Satisfied with his progress, Kent wasted no time.
He immediately began forming his first Lightning Core, believing it would elevate his strength to yet another level.
Four months later, golden-red lightning erupted from Kent’s body, transforming the entire training ground into a domain of crackling lightning.
<Congratulations, you have formed your first Lightning Core.>
Kent smiled in satisfaction.
At last, he had formed every core required for his First Blood Gate. Of course, if he ever developed an affinity for another element or energy in the future, he could always forge additional cores.
But in just six months, he had completely perfected his First Blood Gate.
His attention then shifted to the Second Blood Gate.
To complete it, he needed to forge a second Chaos Heart, Evil Core, Ice Core, and Lightning Core.
Naturally, he chose to begin with the Chaos Heart. There was no better place to cultivate one than a world overflowing with Chaos Essence.
Four months later, the long-awaited notification appeared.
An overwhelming tide of Chaos Essence exploded from Kent’s body. The density of the energy was so terrifying that everyone within the Red Bone Chaos Tribe immediately sensed it.
<Congratulations, you have formed your second Chaos Heart.>
<The rate of Chaos Essence absorption has increased by 3x.>
Kent’s eyes widened.
He could clearly feel the amount of Chaos Essence pouring into his body increase threefold.
"What..."
He was completely bewildered.
Inside the tribe’s central hall, Jyoti Lata and the others had also sensed the disturbance, sending their attention to the purple-haired dragon brat somewhere in their tribe.
Jyoti Lata frowned as she watched the enormous currents of Chaos Essence converging toward Kent’s cultivation ground.
"This child... he’s far more talented than I initially gave him credit for," she muttered.
The others silently nodded.

"Perhaps he truly is related to the Chaos Ascension King," Ragini Disha said, still refusing to let go of the idea that Kent shared some connection with the creator of their race and the absolute ruler of the Chaos Chasm.
"For now, we’ll simply observe," Jyoti Lata replied calmly.

"If he later shows any undeniable signs of being related to the Chaos Ascension King, I’ll inform the leaders of the other tribes. At the end of the day, all of us wish to leave this place. If helping him means helping ourselves, then none of us should hesitate."
The others nodded once more.
What the Red Bone Chaos Tribe didn’t know was that Kent’s existence had already attracted the attention of another Chaos Tribe.
They had already begun tracking him.
Kent then began forging his second Evil Core.
A full year passed.
It had now been roughly two years since he entered secluded cultivation.
Suddenly, an overwhelming wave of sinister energy burst out of his body, spreading across the entire Red Bone Chaos Tribe.
The moment the residents sensed it, countless experts rushed into the skies, weapons drawn.
"Stand down, everyone."
Jyoti Lata’s calm voice echoed throughout the city, instantly stopping everyone in their tracks.
Meanwhile, Kent remained completely unaware of the commotion he had caused.
His attention was fixed on the notifications before him as a smile slowly spread across his face.
<Congratulations, you have formed your second Evil Core.>
<You have awakened the second Evil Key.>
<Your Evil Eye has grown stronger.>
The first notification wasn’t surprising.
Neither was the third.
It was the second one that completely caught him off guard.
’A second Evil Key...’
That meant he could awaken a second Grand Shaman.
The first Evil Key had allowed him to awaken Grand Shaman Malak, who was currently commanding his Beasts and the Evil Legion within the Star Realm.
Now...
He had obtained the key to awaken another one.
To Kent, that was simply unbelievable.
*"Tower, use the second key now,"* Kent commanded.
A moment later, the reply appeared.
<The Master cannot awaken the second Grand Shaman within this world.>
<The Master must first return to his own universe.>
Kent sighed.
Although slightly disappointed, his excitement quickly returned.
’If forming the second Evil Core grants me another Evil Key... then what will happen after I form the third Evil Core?’
The thought alone filled him with anticipation.
Without wasting another moment, he began forging his second Ice Core.
It took eight months.
After completing it, he immediately moved on to his second Lightning Core.
That process also lasted another eight months.
By the end of his fourth year of cultivation, Kent had successfully completed every core required for both his First and Second Blood Gates.
He slowly opened his eyes and clenched his fists, feeling the overwhelming strength flowing throughout his body.
"I’ll spend the next five years tempering my body," he muttered.
"After that, I’ll awaken the Third Blood Gate... and then begin raising my cultivation realm."
