chapters.title: Chapter 1768: Primordial Body Tempering Art
paragraphs: "AhhhhhgggGGGGGG!"

Kent let out a painful scream that seemed to originate from deep within his soul. At once, his skin turned pale red, heat radiating from his body almost as if he were a hot iron that had been dipped into a bucket of water.
In his hand rested a brown-colored fruit.
After months of bathing his body in several concoctions, he had finally gotten to the consumables. However, the first item he consumed proved extremely powerful and severely dangerous.

In fact, the moment the first drop of essence entered his body, he felt as though a wave of lava had been poured into him, causing his internal organs to feel as if they were on an anvil, being hammered into shape.
He gritted his teeth, feeling like his body was about to give up on him.
A few minutes later, despite blood pouring from his eyes and nose, he bit into the fruit again, taking more essence into his body.
The pain intensified, and his body trembled, showing he was at the point where the pain could kill him.
Even so, he persists.
He took the third bite, then the fourth, until the last of the fruit was consumed. By then, he was fully cooked and ready to be eaten. His skin had been baked, steamed, and fried altogether.

"Impressive. This is my first time seeing someone below the Primordial Realm able to consume an Eternal Requiem Fruit in one sitting," Kwame muttered, seated inside the hall with the other Primordials and the two Eternals.
They nodded, sharing the same thoughts.
Indeed, what Kent was doing surpassed what any of them had expected him to be capable of. The fruits and treasures they had given him weren’t things he could underestimate at all.
However, he had asked for them, and they had provided them, so now all they could do was watch him endure the pain.
They had already watched him temper his skin in all kinds of liquids over the past months, so this was just another routine for them. They found it fun to watch him cultivate.
"His pain tolerance is good, but he lacks the cultivation method to refine the essence he has consumed," Jyoti Lata stated, seeing more than the rest could.
She was someone with extensive knowledge of body tempering.

In fact, her tribe was full of body cultivators, so she knew more about body tempering than the six remaining tribes. Watching Kent temper his body, she seemed to understand what he was trying to achieve.
But she also noticed the limitations of his cultivation method. If he were to be tempering his body with ordinary treasures, then his cultivation method would have been enough.
But the treasures here are for Celestials and Primordials.
"Should we share our method with him?" Ragini Disha asked, and the rest turned to Jyoti Lata, who maintained a calm expression despite witnessing something so extraordinary.
Kent was a miracle, and she knew that deep down. More importantly, Kent was now working to help them clear the trail left behind by the Chaos Ascension King.
So helping him achieve that was, at the very least, the least they could do.
"Why not?" she said.
Then she flicked her hand, sending a yellow ball of energy flying toward Kent, who was still doing his best to endure the pain he was going through.
It merged with his forehead, and through the pain, Kent saw the message.
<Jyoti Lata of the Red Bone Chaos Tribe has shared a Primordial Body Tempering Art with you. Do you want to accept and learn?>
[Y/N]
Kent pressed Yes because, just like the 12 leaders in the hall, he also understood his limitations the moment he began absorbing the essence of the Eternal Requiem Fruit.
The moment he pressed Yes, waves of information poured into his mind.
<Congratulations, you have learned the Nine Demon Body Tempering Art.>
<Your Eternal Chaos Dragon Cultivation Art is activating...>
<Your Eternal Chaos Dragon Cultivation Art has activated and is syncing with the Nine Demon Body Tempering Art.>
<Your Eternal Chaos Dragon Cultivation Art has synced with the Nine Demon Body Tempering Art... First Demon Body is being cultivated: 1%.>
Kent felt the essence within him surge like a tide, tempering every part of his body.
It was as though pathways that had been closed—or had never even existed—opened up, allowing more of the essence he had consumed to work its magic.
In no time, the essence from the Eternal Requiem Fruit was depleted, and he picked up another consumable and ate it. Then he went for the next one, and then the one after that.
"Wow, is it just me, or does this kid seem to have an insatiable appetite for tempering fruits?" one of the Primordials, Baychelle, said, noticing how many fruits Kent was consuming.
"The better question should be what changed after he learned the technique. In fact, which technique did you give him, Leader?" Mrinali asked.
"I gave him the Nine Demon Body Tempering Art."
"WHAT?!"
They all exclaimed, not expecting Kent to have already learned perhaps the most complex and strongest Primordial-grade body tempering art they possessed.
"Just how fast is his comprehension speed?" Devak asked, paying much closer attention to Kent, who hadn’t stopped consuming fruits.
In fact, he seemed to be enjoying himself rather than feeling the pain. Now, within a week, he would consume at least ten fruits.
Months went by, and before he realized it, it had been seven years since he started cultivating. Still, he wasn’t done cultivating the First Demon Body.
However, compared to before learning the Nine Demon Body Tempering Art, his body had now become at least 4,000 times more robust. This showed the kind of monster he was becoming.
Two more years passed, bringing the total to nine since he began.
Months after the ninth year, the message appeared, accompanied by a powerful explosion of energy—the kind that caused the very space around him to warp and shatter, revealing the void beyond.
Seated inside the hall, the ten Primordials and two Eternals furrowed their brows as they watched Kent surge with so much power.

"He did it, huh? This kid is a monster," Jyoti Lata said, a smile forming on her beautiful face. Considering how long they had lived, being impressed by someone who wasn’t even considered more than a mortal in their eyes said a lot.
"At this rate, we should add more resources to his stockpile since he’ll most definitely try to cultivate the Second Demon Body." Jyoti Lata added, and the rest of them nodded.
Kent smiled as he watched the messages before him.
<Congratulations, you have successfully cultivated the First Demon Body.>
<You have awakened the first form of the Demon Transformation Art.>
<You have unlocked the Second Demon Body.>
Kent narrowed his eyes at the messages before tapping into the Demon Transformation Art. It is a technique that he can use as he cultivates the Nine Demon Body Tempering Art.
At once, his body surged with power, and his height in his Demi-Dragon form shot up from 7’3" to 7’8".
His muscles grew larger, and his body swelled with immense power. His skin turned a bit metallic, golden, and very hard.
More importantly, Kent felt his body open, allowing him to channel all his energy without restraint.
And he did.

He channeled his Chaos Heart, Evil Core, Flame Core, Blood Core, Ice Core, and Lightning Core, causing his new form to become so densely packed with power that he felt like he could punch a Supreme to death.
"This power..."
He clenched his fist and threw a punch.
BOOM! CRACK!
The space before him fractured, and the void beyond was exposed, demonstrating that the force behind the punch was simply too overwhelming to comprehend.
Kent felt it deep within him—a power he had never experienced before—surging through his body and urging him to throw more punches.
And he did.
He unleashed punch after punch, each one shattering the void and making the surrounding space increasingly unstable.
"Damn, at this rate, I might just end up becoming a monster before leaving this place," he said with a smile as he deactivated the Demon Transformation Art.

In no time, the essence from the Eternal Requiem Fruit was depleted, and he picked up another consumable and ate it.
Then he went for the next one, and then the one after that.
"Wow, is it just me, or does this kid seem to have an insatiable appetite for tempering fruits?" one of the Primordials, Baychelle, said, noticing how many fruits Kent was consuming.
"The better question should be what changed after he learned the technique.
In fact, which technique did you give him, Leader?" Mrinali asked.
"I gave him the Nine Demon Body Tempering Art."
"WHAT?!"
They all exclaimed, not expecting Kent to have already learned perhaps the most complex and strongest Primordial-grade body tempering art they possessed.
"Just how fast is his comprehension speed?" Devak asked, paying much closer attention to Kent, who hadn’t stopped consuming fruits.
In fact, he seemed to be enjoying himself rather than feeling the pain.
Now, within a week, he would consume at least ten fruits.
Months went by, and before he realized it, it had been seven years since he started cultivating.
Still, he wasn’t done cultivating the First Demon Body.
However, compared to before learning the Nine Demon Body Tempering Art, his body had now become at least 4,000 times more robust.
This showed the kind of monster he was becoming.
Two more years passed, bringing the total to nine since he began.
Months after the ninth year, the message appeared, accompanied by a powerful explosion of energy—the kind that caused the very space around him to warp and shatter, revealing the void beyond.
Seated inside the hall, the ten Primordials and two Eternals furrowed their brows as they watched Kent surge with so much power.
"He did it, huh?
This kid is a monster," Jyoti Lata said, a smile forming on her beautiful face.
Considering how long they had lived, being impressed by someone who wasn’t even considered more than a mortal in their eyes said a lot.
"At this rate, we should add more resources to his stockpile since he’ll most definitely try to cultivate the Second Demon Body." Jyoti Lata added, and the rest of them nodded.
Kent smiled as he watched the messages before him.
<Congratulations, you have successfully cultivated the First Demon Body.>
<You have awakened the first form of the Demon Transformation Art.>
<You have unlocked the Second Demon Body.>
Kent narrowed his eyes at the messages before tapping into the Demon Transformation Art.
It is a technique that he can use as he cultivates the Nine Demon Body Tempering Art.
At once, his body surged with power, and his height in his Demi-Dragon form shot up from 7’3" to 7’8".
His muscles grew larger, and his body swelled with immense power.
His skin turned a bit metallic, golden, and very hard.
More importantly, Kent felt his body open, allowing him to channel all his energy without restraint.
And he did.

He channeled his Chaos Heart, Evil Core, Flame Core, Blood Core, Ice Core, and Lightning Core, causing his new form to become so densely packed with power that he felt like he could punch a Supreme to death.
"This power..."
He clenched his fist and threw a punch.
BOOM!
CRACK!
The space before him fractured, and the void beyond was exposed, demonstrating that the force behind the punch was simply too overwhelming to comprehend.
Kent felt it deep within him—a power he had never experienced before—surging through his body and urging him to throw more punches.
And he did.
He unleashed punch after punch, each one shattering the void and making the surrounding space increasingly unstable.
"Damn, at this rate, I might just end up becoming a monster before leaving this place," he said with a smile as he deactivated the Demon Transformation Art.

chapters.title: Chapter 1769: Body Tempering Prodigy
paragraphs: It’s been eleven years since Kent began cultivating in the Chaos Chasm, within the territory of the Red Bone Chaos Tribe.
So far, he had formed two cores for each of his affinities—the Blood Core, Chaos Heart, Evil Core, Flame Core, Ice Core, and Lightning Core.
Aside from that, he had also tempered his body to such an extent that, after years of relentless hard work, he was now comparable to a Supreme Lord walking the body tempering path.
He had already attained the First Demon Body in the Nine Demon Body Tempering Art. However, that wasn’t good enough for Kent.
After achieving such a breakthrough—one that would have taken many years under normal circumstances—he immediately moved on to cultivate the Second Demon Body.
His plan was to cultivate up to the Third Demon Body, since he could already tell that attempting it in his own universe would consume all his wealth.
The treasures required to cultivate the Second Demon Body alone were simply too numerous and precious to comprehend.
So he intended to take full advantage of the opportunity he had been given and cultivate three Demon Bodies before the fifty years were up.
Then again, if only he knew what was coming.ree

Kent was well aware that as long as the fifty years hadn’t ended, he would never lack cultivation treasures. So he devoted himself wholeheartedly to cultivation, repeatedly shocking the leaders and people of the Red Bone Chaos Tribe.
Aside from the twelve leaders, the tribe had roughly forty thousand members, with even the weakest being three teenagers, each at the Supreme Monarch stage.
If Kent were to meet them, he would probably call them his juniors. Yet a single punch from any one of them would be enough to shatter every bone in his body.
Amazingly, every one of them paid close attention to Kent, whom their leaders had already announced would be representing their tribe in the upcoming Chaos Ascension King Trial.
Because of this, they all regarded him as someone of great importance to their tribe.
The Chaos Ascension King Trial is open to anyone from the Demigod stage onward to participate.

This also meant that the trial was different for every participant, by adapting to their cultivation level. So, despite Kent being only an Immortal Monarch, they knew it was only a matter of time before he reached the Demigod stage.
[12 Years into Cultivation]

On the twelve year since he had begun cultivating, the first person from another tribe arrived, having followed the signs that had appeared over the years while Kent cultivated within the Red Bone Chaos Tribe.
The first sign appeared when he formed his second Chaos Heart. Everyone felt a power so vast and untamed spread throughout the Chaos Chasm.
At first, it was attributed to someone making a breakthrough in the Chaos Chasm.
However, the moment the auras of Ice, Flame, Lightning, Evil, and his other affinities began spreading across the world, they realized something extraordinary was happening within their realm.
The Tribe Leader of the Void Vein Chaos Tribe, Borislav, arrived after traveling several light-years to reach the Red Bone Chaos Tribe.

The Chaos Chasm might be a single world with only seven tribes, each containing fewer than one hundred thousand people, but it was unimaginably vast. Traveling from one tribe to another could take several million light-years.

However, since even the weakest inhabitant of this world was a Demigod, Borislav arrived in less than five minutes. The only thing that took time was tracking the source of the unusual energy fluctuations.

"I never expected the Red Bone Chaos Tribe to have produced such a prodigy in recent years. It makes me wonder when it happened and why I haven’t heard of it sooner," Borislav said, his voice echoing directly into the minds of the twelve leaders of the Red Bone Chaos Tribe.
Jyoti Lata smiled when she heard him. She rose from her throne before appearing beside her.
"I thought you and your people wanted nothing to do with us ever again. Did I hear wrong, or has your shamelessness simply given you thicker skin?" Jyoti Lata replied, maintaining her smile.

While she possessed a more proportionate height compared to the rest of her tribe, who possessed towering heights standing between eight and eleven feet tall, with crimson-white bones naturally visible beneath translucent skin, two large curved horns, red glowing veins carrying liquid Chaos Essence, and golden-red eyes with slit pupils—the Tribe Leader of the Void Vein Chaos Tribe had a much leaner appearance.
He had pale gray skin that shimmered beneath the twin suns overhead, long silver-black hair, and black sclera surrounding deep purple irises.
Four metallic Chaos Rings floated behind his back, and, most notably, his thin, elegant physique stood in stark contrast to the towering builds of the Red Bone Chaos Tribe.
Instead of horns, two crystalline Chaos antennae extended from his temples.

"You can’t blame me for that when it was your tribe’s fault to begin with. One hundred thousand years ago, a member of your tribe killed someone from mine, so blame your inability to keep your people under control," Borislav laughed before turning his gaze toward the area where Kent was cultivating.
Like Jyoti Lata, he was also a True Eternal, a being who had already surpassed the Primordial Realm.
"He doesn’t look like one of yours, Jyoti Lata."
"That’s because he isn’t. He came from the Infinity Universe."
Borislav furrowed his brows.
"Now that is interesting. The last time someone came from there was... what, ten billion years ago?"

"Thirteen and a half billion years ago, and that person is now an Eternal like us. So you can imagine my joy when he appeared in my tribe," Jyoti Lata said with a laugh, taking the opportunity to brag a little.
For as long as she could remember, no one from the Infinity Universe had ever arrived within her tribe. In fact, she had performed countless rituals over the years, yet none had yielded results.
So, finally receiving one of her own made her genuinely happy.
"He arrived sixteen years ago, and you can already see the progress he has made."
Borislav nodded.
"Not only does he possess the physique of a Supreme Lord, but he also has more than one Chaos Heart. On top of that, he’s close to attaining the Second Demon Body."
He turned to look at Jyoti Lata.
"This kid is a body tempering prodigy."
Jyoti Lata laughed.
"Indeed. It took me thirteen thousand years to attain the Second Demon Body, yet he’s about to accomplish it in less than twenty years. It makes me wonder if he’s the one we’ve all been waiting for."
"You don’t mean..."
Borislav looked at Kent once more, this time examining him much more carefully. When he sensed the other aura surrounding Kent, his eyes widened.
"This... Is he related to the Chaos Ascension King?"

"He said no, but I still have my doubts. Regardless, he has agreed to represent my tribe in the upcoming Chaos Ascension King Trial. So if he truly is the one destined to grant us our freedom, then a few years from now, he’ll prove it to us."
"Even if he isn’t, I’d still put my money on a monster like him."
Jyoti Lata smiled faintly.
"Oh? Are you planning on snatching him away from me?"
Borislav smirked.
"Don’t be ridiculous, Jyoti Lata. At the end of the day, if he passes the trial, all seven of us will gain our freedom. So if anything, I’d rather help him achieve that."
’Of course you would. Otherwise, I wouldn’t have baited you suckers into coming here,’ Jyoti Lata laughed inwardly, turning slightly to her left, looking into the distance.

chapters.title: Chapter 1770: Leaders of the Chaos Chasm
paragraphs: The moment Jyoti Lata heard what Borislav said, she knew it was time to implement her perfectly elaborate plan.
Deep within, she trusted and believed Kent would be able to free them from the Chaos Chasm.
She reached this conclusion because, aside from Kent, nobody from her world and those from the Infinity Universe who had come to the Chaos Chasm possessed more than two cores.
More importantly, no one else possessed two Chaos Hearts. It was her first time seeing such an anomaly, and because of that, she trusted and believed Kent would be able to help them.

The second reason, and perhaps the most important one, was that she had come to this conclusion because of the deductions she had made over the years while experiencing the Chaos Ascension King Trial.
In the last four trials, she had seen that, aside from the first level, none of the participants had advanced to the second level.
Of course, once someone failed the trial, all memories of what had transpired inside it would be wiped from their mind. So she had no idea what they had seen and experienced.
However, she was wise enough to draw some conclusions. Her most serious conclusion was that the trial had seven trials, each representing one of the tribes.
This meant the only person who could pass the trial would be someone who could wield the cultivation art of all seven tribes.
The Chaos Ascension King left a powerful cultivation art for each tribe, and so she believed that to pass his trial, one person should be able to wield all seven cultivation arts.

Kent had proven himself so far, making her see him as worthy of such a chance. Most importantly, Kent could perhaps be the only one capable of wielding both the cultivation art of her tribe and that of the other tribes.
Since that was the case and because every being in the Chaos Chasm desired their freedom, she baited the other tribe leaders into coming to her tribe to witness Kent in action.

While the energy produced by Kent’s cultivation was potent, it was not strong enough for beings millions of light-years away to sense it. So she amplified it, making sure it reached them just enough to pique their interest.
Borislav, the leader of the Void Vein Chaos Tribe, was the first to arrive.
A few hours after he arrived, the second tribe leader came. He was from the Obsidian Scale Chaos Tribe, the third-strongest tribe in the Chaos Chasm.
"It appears there is something good happening here if Borislav of all people came before me," said Veylan Seren, the tribe leader of the Obsidian Scale Chaos Tribe.
Just like the beings of the Red Bone Chaos Tribe, he was also a towering man, standing about ten feet tall, with jet-black skin covered in obsidian dragon scales.
Massive horns protruded from his forehead, and four glowing red eyes lined his face perfectly.
He appeared to be in his late fifties but possessed a fit, muscular physique.
Just like Jyoti Lata and Borislav, he was also a True Eternal.

The only reason his tribe was the third strongest was that, aside from him, there was another True Eternal and a Real Eternal, bringing the total number of Eternals in the Obsidian Scale Chaos Tribe to three.
This surpassed both the Red Bone Chaos Tribe and the Void Vein Chaos Tribe, which only had two each.

"I never expected old Veylan Seren to come this fast. The last I checked, I was told you broke your back by biting off more than you could chew," Borislav said with a laugh, causing Veylan Seren to smirk.
"Unlike you, who enjoys the comfort of your throne, I actually go out there fighting the terrifying creaures of the Void from swallowing our world."
Borislav sneered and responded, "Nobody sent you, old man."
Veylan Seren simply brushed him off and turned to Jyoti Lata.
"Looks like you have found yourself a gem, Jyoti Lata."
"More like he found me, but I’ll take the compliment," she laughed, looking at Kent as he took another consumable and swallowed it.
"Are you training him to challenge the Chaos Ascension King Trial?" Veylan Seren asked.
Jyoti Lata nodded.

"That’s right. He is from the Infinity Universe, just like that lady in your tribe who came millions of years ago. But unlike her, this kid has the constitution to wield all seven Arts left behind by the Chaos Ascension King."

"Oh, so that was why you called us here," Veylan Seren said, a smile appearing on his face. "It appears you want to bet everything on him, even going as far as giving him the infamous Nine Demon Body Tempering Art."

"I am not easily impressed, Veylan Seren, so naturally, he seems to have earned a place in my mind. For now, you can watch, and if you are satisfied with what you see, you can contribute to his growth. Also, it would be good if you could summon that lady in your tribe."
"You think she would recognize him?"
"I don’t know, but she did mention a Chaos Dragon before, and this kid is a dragon who possesses Chaos Energy, so it is worth checking."
"Very well."
Veylan Seren sent a message to his tribe before turning his attention back to Kent, who was now cultivating the second Demon Body.
A day later, the third tribe leader arrived.
"Hmm, I guess I came to the right place," said Zdzislav, the tribe leader of the Astral Eye Chaos Tribe, as he walked out of a void gate with an elegant posture.
He stood about seven feet tall, with indigo skin, the kind that made him stand out even among the other tribe leaders.
He had six glowing eyes, while a ring of floating cosmic eye tattoos hovered behind his back. His hair resembled flowing starlight. Undoubtedly, he was exceptionally handsome.
He also has a True Eternal Cultivation base.
"If it isn’t the man with the unpronounceable name," Borislav joked.
Zdzislav immediately became annoyed by the bastard who seemed to find humor in everything.
"Stay out of my business, Borislav."
He walked toward Jyoti Lata, on whom he clearly had a crush.
"Jyoti Lata, dear, I hope you’ve been well," he said, sounding unusually friendly and flirtatious.

"Tch, what a hopeless bastard," Borislav muttered with a smirk before turning his attention back to Kent, who had no idea he had already begun attracting some of the most terrifying cultivators in the Chaos Chasm.
Jyoti Lata ignored Zdzislav. She knew he would not mind acting shameless if it meant getting even the slightest smile from her.
She had learned to ignore him a billion years ago.
Luckily, only a few minutes after Zdzislav arrived, the fourth tribe leader also appeared.
This time, it was a woman, and she arrived with an overwhelming presence that clearly showed she had long since broken through to the Eternal King Realm.
She was Parand, the tribe leader of the Storm Wing Chaos Tribe.
Like Zdzislav, she possessed an average height, standing at 6’7", with blue-grey skin that gave her an alien yet strangely human appearance. Long jet-black hair flowed gracefully down her back.

Four enormous feathered Chaos Wings spread majestically from her back. If Kent were to see those wings, his eyes would undoubtedly widen in surprise. Although he possessed only three pairs, his Jade Void Wings looked almost identical to Parand’s.
Lightning tattoos traced elegant patterns across her skin, while crown-like horns extended from her forehead.
"Zdzislav, sometimes you should just take the hint and know when someone says no. Or do you want me to smack the word ’NO’ into your skull?" Parand said, flashing a beautiful smile.

If Kent were to see those wings, his eyes would undoubtedly widen in surprise.
Although he possessed only three pairs, his Jade Void Wings looked almost identical to Parand’s.
Lightning tattoos traced elegant patterns across her skin, while crown-like horns extended from her forehead.
"Zdzislav, sometimes you should just take the hint and know when someone says no.
Or do you want me to smack the word ’NO’ into your skull?" Parand said, flashing a beautiful smile.

chapters.title: Chapter 1771: Shocking The Seven Tribe Leaders
paragraphs: Parand is undoubtedly one of the strongest tribe leaders in the Chaos Chasm. Her tribe ranks second and is perhaps the most dangerous when certain factors are taken into consideration.
They specialize in speed, and their Storm Wings allow them to harness the power of Storm Chaos.
She is an Eternal King, unlike the rest, who are all True Eternals. Her arrival alone caused everyone to behave themselves.
Zdzislav, who had initially wanted to pester Jyoti Lata, immediately backed off, knowing he couldn’t act recklessly in front of Parand.
"Thanks for the assist, Parand," Jyoti Lata said, sounding relieved that she wouldn’t have to deal with Zdzislav anymore.
"Just get stronger, and you’ll be able to shoo him away anytime. He used to bother me the same way until I became an Eternal King. After that, he backed off like the little coward he is."
Zdzislav, who had just taken a jab, simply smiled and replied, "Eternal King for now. Just give me a few million years, and I’ll be standing right beside you."
Parand smirked but said nothing, as her attention had already shifted to Kent, who was much closer to attaining a second demon body.
"Well, there’s always someone with untamed potential hiding somewhere."
She turned to Jyoti Lata and asked, "Where did you find this monster?"
Jyoti Lata smiled and replied, "He came from the Infinity Universe."
"Well, that’s unexpected, but I suppose that also explains everything about him."
She had already seen through Kent and knew he possessed more than one core, something that made her wonder just what kind of monster he truly was.
"I suppose you called us here because of him."
Jyoti Lata nodded, unsurprised that Parand had seen through her intentions.
"I am impressed already, but we’ll have to wait for Namarie and Tumenk."

A few hours into their wait, the tribe leader of the Eternal Root Chaos Tribe arrived in all her glory. She possessed emerald skin that shimmered beneath the twin suns in the sky and hair resembling glowing vines.
As a member of a race that specialized in manipulating plants, she bore a striking resemblance to the Plantkins.
She had emerald-green eyes, long verdant hair, and wooden antlers growing from her forehead.
Crystal flowers bloomed across parts of her skin, making her appear even more elegant. She was Namarie, the most harmless-looking yet most dangerous tribe leader.

Her tribe specialized in healing, but just as they could give life, they could also take it away. They were ranked seventh in the Chaos Chasm, yet everyone knew that if they ever went berserk, the consequences would be catastrophic.
After she arrived, the last tribe leader followed.

He was Tumenk, the tribe leader of the Celestial Abyss Chaos Tribe, the strongest tribe in the entire Chaos Chasm, and the most powerful tribe leader, having reached the peak of the Eternal Emperor stage.
Just like Veylan Seren, he possessed midnight-black skin covered in ever-shifting galaxy tattoos. Four enormous spiral horns rose from his forehead, looking both imposing and surprisingly elegant.
He had glowing white eyes, while floating Chaos runes orbited his massive body. Standing well over nine feet tall, his mere presence radiated overwhelming pressure.
"Jyoti Lata, it seems you’ve been hiding quite the gem within your tribe," Tumenk said as he calmly walked toward the tribe leader of the Red Bone Chaos Tribe.
"Hiding him is such a strong word, don’t you think, Tumenk?"
Tumenk smiled and shook his head. "Whatever. Now, what I’m interested in is why you called for us, Jyoti Lata. I was in the middle of something extremely important, so this had better be worth it."
Jyoti Lata nodded and was about to speak when another figure appeared.
She was an elf, judging by her pointed ears and extraordinary beauty. Unlike the others, she stood only 6’2" tall, making it obvious she wasn’t native to this world.
Everyone turned to look at her.

Thirteen billion years ago, she had fallen out of a Chaos Portal similar to the one Kent entered after shattering his Chaos Heart. However, whether it had been an accident or not, she arrived in this world.

She had arrived with the same story as many others before her. Before the portal appeared, she was in the middle of a terrifying battle, moments away from death, when a portal suddenly opened and pulled her into this place.
She was accepted in the hope that she would pass the Chaos Ascension King Trial, but she failed, just like many others.

Even so, her talent was so extraordinary that in just thirteen billion years, she had advanced from the Celestial Stage to the Real Eternal Stage, proving just how exceptional she was in this new world.
"Fiannarel, it’s good to see you again," Jyoti Lata said, greeting the elven lady.
Fiannarel smiled and was about to respond when a wave of power burst forth from the direction where Kent was cultivating.
Turning slightly, her eyes narrowed before suddenly widening.
"No way," she muttered, immediately drawing the attention of everyone gathered.
"B-Brother..."
She stared intently at Kent.
"Fiannarel, do you recognize this kid?" Veylan Seren asked, bringing her attention back to the group.
"I’m not sure, but I think he might be the person I told you about," Fiannarel replied, turning her gaze back to Kent, who was on the verge of completing his second demon body.
"Right, the archer who could supposedly see the past and the future," Zdzislav said sarcastically.
Fiannarel simply smiled and nodded.
"He was the greatest warrior I had ever known from the day I first picked up a bow."
Her smile softened as she continued to gaze at Kent, still uncertain whether he truly was the person she had missed for so long.
"We called him the Omniscience Dao Archer... but he was also my brother. My little brother, to be precise."
The seven tribe leaders widened their eyes.
Jyoti Lata asked, "So, if what you’re saying is true, then this kid might be the reincarnation of your brother, since I doubt he was a dragon back when you were both still in the Infinity Universe."
Fiannarel, who had been so focused on the familiar aura surrounding Kent that she had ignored his draconic features, finally noticed the horns protruding from his head. Her eyes narrowed once more.
"I’m not sure, but I feel a connection with him. Until he awakens, all I can do is hope."
"Then tell us," Jyoti Lata continued, "if this kid really is your brother, what are his chances of passing the Chaos Ascension King Trial?"
At Jyoti Lata’s question, Fiannarel smiled.
"When I said the Omniscience Dao Archer was the greatest warrior I had ever known, I meant among everyone—including all seven of you."
Her smile widened.
"So you can only imagine why I still hold on to that belief even after witnessing an entirely different world here."
Fiannarel’s words drew the seven tribe leaders’ attention to Kent with renewed interest.
As though he had sensed their attention, Kent chose that exact moment to make his breakthrough.
BOOM!
A terrifying wave of power erupted from his body, blending the auras of Chaos, Blood, Evil, Ice, Fire, and Lightning into a single overwhelming force.
All seven tribe leaders felt the hairs on the backs of their necks stand on end.
Their eyes widened in disbelief.

Fiannarel clenched her fists, desperately hoping the connection she felt was real—not simply because she and Kent came from the same universe, but because she wanted her little brother to have truly returned.
<Congratulations. You have successfully cultivated the Second Demon Body.>
<You have awakened the second form of the Demon Transformation Art.>

chapters.title: Chapter 1772: Decision of the Seven Tribe Leaders
paragraphs: Kent stood 7’4" tall, his body covered in golden draconic scales. Every single scale was engraved with millions of tiny runes, each one brimming with unimaginable power.

If before he looked like nothing more than a dragon-man blessed with an incredible physique and overwhelming strength, then now he appeared both elegant and terrifying, carrying a presence that would, without a shred of doubt, make even Supremes and some Celestials tremble.
He had not grown larger or more muscular, yet his scales now radiated an overwhelming aura of immense power and unfathomable mystery.
"This power..." Kent muttered as he slowly reached forward with a single finger. With an almost casual motion, he gently tapped the air before him, as though he were touching an invisible wall.

However, that simple tap shattered the space before him. It was as though a devastating warhammer had struck reality itself, sending countless spiderweb-like cracks racing through the surrounding space.
"This..." His eyes widened.
Inside the hall, the seven tribe leaders and Fiannarel also raised their brows.
It had to be noted that although the Nine Demon Body Tempering Art was one of the greatest body-tempering techniques in the entire Chaos Chasm, Kent was still merely an Immortal Monarch.
Yet the power he had displayed was so terrifying that even True Supremes would struggle to replicate it.
In fact, only thirty percent of his strength had gone into shattering space and exposing the void. What, then, would happen if he unleashed more... or even all of his power?
"Should I continue cultivating the Third Demon Body, or should I switch back to raising my cultivation since I have more than enough Blood Essence?" Kent thought, weighing his options.
’Tower, how long has it been since I started cultivating?’
<Master has been cultivating for thirteen years so far.>
’So I still have thirty-seven years to go.’
With a clear timeline in mind, he finalized his next course of action.
"I’ll raise my cultivation to the Demigod stage, awaken the Third Blood Gate, form the next set of cores, and then return to cultivating the Third Demon Body."
Kent sat down, took out thousands of Blood Essences, and began absorbing them. Before long, his cultivation advanced from Immortal Monarch to Immortal Lord.

"I don’t know what kind of constitution this kid possesses, but I think his potential surpasses even that of most of us," Tribe Leader Veylan Seren said as he watched Kent’s cultivation rise at an astonishing pace.
Parand nodded before saying, "Perhaps he really is connected to the Chaos Ascension King. His potential closely matches what was recorded in the ancient records.
This kid possesses monstrous talent, and considering he hasn’t even become a god yet but can already contend with Supremes, perhaps we should place our bets on him."
Jyoti Lata smiled and immediately supported Parand.
"I think so too. In fact, my theory about the Trial’s true nature may prove correct if we all work together to help him to pass.
"If he turns out not to be the one destined to free us, then we will still gain an ally who may one day transcend the realm of a Universe God and seek out the Chaos Ascension King himself.
"However, if he succeeds in passing the trials, then we will not only gain our freedom but also an ally whose interests will forever align with ours.

"It all depends on whether we are willing to place our collective trust in him. One thing I know for certain is that he is eager to return home, and because of that, he is willing to devote everything necessary to make it happen."

The six tribe leaders all took deep breaths, their gazes fixed on Kent. Each of them had something unique to offer, and unless they accepted Jyoti Lata’s proposal, Kent would never be able to benefit from those opportunities.
After thinking for a while, Namarie spoke.

"At this point, we can only consider whether or not he has the potential to learn all seven techniques. While he has already proven himself to me, that doesn’t necessarily mean he has the potential to master the rest of our techniques.
"So, we have to consider that first before making a decision."
"He can do it," Fiannarel said confidently. "Call it a gut feeling, but I believe he can."
The seven tribe leaders looked at her for a few moments before letting out another deep sigh.
Namarie was the first to speak again.

"Well, it isn’t as though we have anything to lose by giving him our techniques. Besides, as Jyoti Lata said, we lose nothing yet have everything to gain if he passes the trial. Therefore, my Eternal Root Chaos Tribe will contribute the [World Root Chaos Scripture] to this cause."
"The Red Bone Chaos Tribe will also contribute the [Red Bone Chaos Devouring Art]," Jyoti Lata added.
"I suppose the Storm Wing Chaos Tribe will contribute the [Heaven Splitting Chaos Wings] as well," Parand said, and one after another, the remaining tribe leaders voiced their agreement.

They all believed that, regardless of the outcome, the decision would ultimately benefit them. Thus, they chose to entrust Kent with their most precious inheritances, the Universe grade techniques left behind by the Chaos Ascension King.
Meanwhile, weeks quickly passed.
Kent, who had been cultivating without pause, steadily raised his cultivation from the Immortal Lord stage all the way to the Peak Immortal Lord realm.
He was only a few Blood Essences away from breaking through to the Demigod realm.
However, before doing so, he decided to address another aspect of his cultivation.
After advancing from Immortal Monarch to Immortal Lord, he had awakened so many Blood Runes that he knew it was time to cultivate the Third Form of the Bone Tempering Art.
So he studied the technique to understand everything.
After comprehending it, he realized that, unlike before, he could now advance to the Demigod realm and awaken the Third Blood Gate without first forming another Blood Tattoo.
Since that was the case, he no longer hesitated.
His cultivation erupted.
Soon, an overwhelming aura of divinity began radiating from his body.
A few hours later, a series of notifications appeared before him, and all seven tribe leaders, along with every member of the Red Bone Chaos Tribe, immediately sensed the transformation.
<You have become a Demigod.>
<You have sensed a strand of Divine Qi and started to comprehend it.>
<You have encountered a bottleneck. Awaken the Third Blood Gate to continue leveling up.>
<Because you have reached a bottleneck, Blood Tempering has been activated.>
<Consume more Blood Essence to temper your blood.>
<Current Blood Rank: Monarch>
<Current Progress: 25%>
Kent waved his hand.
In an instant, countless Blood Essences appeared before him. Like a starving lion devouring its prey, he began absorbing them to temper his blood.
When he had formed his first Chaos Heart, he had tempered his blood to the Monarch rank. Every one of his Blood Runes had since turned a brilliant golden color, signifying their Monarch status.
However, the moment Blood Tempering began once more, those golden runes slowly started changing.
Ten days later...
A terrifying wave of power erupted from Kent’s body, sending chills down everyone’s spine.
The seven tribe leaders and Fiannarel instantly rose to their feet, every instinct in their bodies screaming for them to bow before the overwhelming presence pouring from Kent.
<You have fulfilled the requirements to evolve your blood to the Third Evolution Stage.>
Kent stared at the message hovering before him in disbelief.
This was something he had never expected to achieve so early.
For ordinary beasts, evolving their bloodline from the Monarch rank to the Overlord rank often required millions of years of accumulation.
Yet today...
Kent Madson, the Primordial Chaos Dragon, had ascended into the rank of an Overlord.

chapters.title: Chapter 1773: Emotional Reunion
paragraphs: [Congratulations, your blood has evolved to the next stage: Golden-red Overlord Blood]
Kent remained seated, his eyes widened as he stared at the message before him. The idea that he was now an Overlord just seemed to strike him as a prank.

He was a beast, and so he understood that reaching this stage required a lot. Overlords were beings whose presence commanded absolute respect. No matter how weak they might be, their aura alone could compel just about anyone to bow before them.
Kent had even read that Overlords became more powerful as more beasts submitted to them. So, to be an Overlord was to be someone whose authority was absolute and strong enough to lead.
In his past life, Chaos had only reached the Monarch stage, but even then, he was respected by the people he led into many battles.
Now, he was an Overlord, and just as his blood had evolved to that of an Overlord, his bloodline started to awaken beyond the stage it was before coming to this world.
Back when he formed his first Chaos Heart in the Infinity Universe, his bloodline had risen to 35% awakened. Now, it had started to rise.
In only a few minutes, it rose by 5%.
But with that 5% increase, his presence became even more lethal to comprehend.
Suddenly, Kent felt some people appear behind him. He first closed the panel, stood up, then turned, hoping to see Jyoti Lata and the rest of the leaders of the Red Bone Chaos Tribe.
However, when his gaze landed on the seven tribe leaders, he felt his body tremble. Before panic could set in, his aura flared, and the fear vanished.
<You are immune to all forms of intimidation from Eternals and below>
The message brought a smile to his face. However, before he could address the seven leaders, Fiannarel appeared, and the moment their gazes met, Kent froze.
For five full minutes, he stood motionless, his gaze locked intently on Fiannarel. But while he was frozen, Fiannarel was also rooted to the spot, tears rolling down her face.
Then, suddenly, they both moved, tears streaming down their faces. In what could be considered the most emotional reunion ever, Fiannarel jumped into Kent’s arms.
Perhaps if Kent had chosen his human form, he would have been the one to jump into Fiannarel’s arms, since they are almost at the same height.
"Big sister," Kent said, tears rolling down his face.
Seeing this, the seven tribe leaders left the scene to give the siblings a chance to catch up.

Just now, the moment Kent and Fiannarel gazed at each other, his mind was flooded with memories of the life he had lived during the Sun Era, the era that witnessed one of the greatest wars and the rise of the greatest warrior ever to wield the bow.
They called him the Omniscience Dao Archer, an Elven Prince, and the beloved son of the wisest Elven Empress in the history of the universe.
He was the youngest of four siblings and the one who led the battle against the Sun Demons, completely annihilating them down to the last warrior.

The Omniscience Dao Archer was someone with the sight to see both the past and the future and shoot his arrow either way. In other words, he could kill his opponents by firing his arrows into the past, present, or future.

His existence made no sense. In fact, his overpowered nature completely contracted his image in many minds. It was common knowledge that, while growing up, aside from jumping from one woman to another, he was basically useless...
Ir turned out that was the image he showed everyone...
Everyone except one person, his big sister, Fiannarel.
She was already a general in the Elven Army and highly respected.
One day, a rumor began spreading that she had a second identity, called Scarlet Fingers.
During the Sun Era, Elven merchants who traded with other races began encountering bandits while transporting goods from one planet to another.
When this started, many merchants hired guards to protect them, but every time, the bandits got the better of them.
That was until someone mysterious started helping them. Initially, no one suspected General Fiannarel, who preferred to be called General rather than Princess.
However, as more people experienced the devastating power of this mysterious archer, they began to wonder whether it was General Fiannarel, known for her impeccable bow skills.
Soon, many began spreading the word that General Fiannarel was the Scarlet Fingers.
However, when she heard this and realized she was not the one, she began searching for the person behind it. Soon, she realized she was making no progress, so she decided to disguise herself.
She disguised herself as a merchant, and that day, she finally came face to face with the Scarlet Fingers, who, to her shock, was her useless brother, using her name and skills to get out of trouble.
She was so shocked that she nearly collapsed. But when she recovered and questioned him, she found out her brother desired peace, but he also hated seeing their people die at the hands of bandits.
So he created a secret identity to help.
When she questioned how he could wield the bow like a pro yet she had never seen him train, considering he spends most of his time chasing ladies or sleeping, his answer left her jaw hanging.
"I train in my dreams, big sister. Whenever I sleep, I find myself on battlefields where I have to fight, or else I wake up feeling like I’ve been hammered into submission. So I train in my sleep."
She knew her brother desired peace, so she made him her Shadow General. This way, he could serve in the army while continuing to live his carefree life.
However, when the Sun Demons came and death spread everywhere, the Omniscience Dao Archer appeared and changed everything.
The entire universe witnessed what he was capable of, and Fiannarel finally saw the kind of person her little brother truly was.

Seeing him carry the entire universe on his back, she made a vow to ensure he succeeds and has a happy ending. That was why, during the war, when the danger reached a certain point, she decided to go all out with no intention of failing.
In the end, instead of death, she survived and found herself transported to a strange world.

For the first few million years, she blamed herself, feeling like a deserter. After all, she had promised her brother that she would stand by his side until the very end. If she had died, she would not have blamed herself, for she had given it her all.
However, she survived, and what was even worse was that she could not return to her world, no matter how hard she tried. That had eaten away at her sanity for years.
However, over time, she came to accept her new life.
Never in her wildest dreams did she think the brother she had thought about every single day for the past 13 billion years would now be in her arms.
"Is it really you, Kalimndra?"
She asked, referring to Kent by the name he was known by during the Sun Era.
"It is me, big sister. I missed you so much," Kent replied, causing the hug to become even tighter and incredibly soul-soothing.

The siblings who had once stood on the same battlefield, making plans for what they would do after the war ended, only to be separated before they could fulfill any of them, had now reunited in an emotional reunion—one that was never meant to happen in this life or the next.

The idea that he was now an Overlord just seemed to strike him as a prank.

chapters.title: Chapter 1774: Tell Me Everything
paragraphs: Unlike Kent’s past life as Kevin Sage, who hated his siblings from his mother’s side, Kalimndra, the lazy prince whom many looked down on, loved his big sister dearly.
She had protected him when many thought he was useless. And when she discovered his secret identity, she didn’t expose him as most people would have.
She understood him and knew letting him continue as he was would be helpful to him. So for several years, Kalimndra maintained his peace.

Because of this, he had grown grateful to her, and so when he saw her get pulled into an unfamiliar portal, Kalimndra became so furious that he went all out, breaking his limits and unlocking so much power that by the time he reached a certain point of power, everyone had stopped fighting and simply watched him decimate the Sun Demons until the very last one.
Everyone has their reverse scale.

Kalimndra’s reverse scale was Fiannarel, who was both overprotective of him and his biggest inspiration. So Chaos Dragon or not, his emotions ran wild, and for ten full minutes, he simply embraced his sister.

Tribe Leader Zdzislav, who was known for his player lifestyle, could only sigh, wishing he were in Kent’s position, hugging such a beauty. Too bad for him, because Kent would never allow a bastard like him to come near his sister.
In fact, if he tried, he would be the first Eternal in history to fall to the claws of a Demigod Dragon.
After ten full minutes of emotional reunion, Kent pulled back and stared his sister in the eye, almost as if to make sure she was indeed her.
While he had changed due to reincarnation, she remained the same, only much more beautiful.

Just like most Elves, she possessed long silver hair with strands of red running through it. She had pale white skin, a testament to her affinity for the Everlasting Dream Sacred Flame, which was naturally white.

She stood with an athletic physique and broad hips, perfectly capturing her striking figure. Her ruby-like blue eyes, of course, had left many wondering whether a person could be both beautiful in shape and in the eyes.
She was gorgeous by all standards.
Kent, after confirming she was indeed the person he had missed for years, hugged her again. This time, it lasted only a few minutes before he pulled back once more.
"Big sister," Kent said, looking back at her with an emotional expression...
Fiannarel smiled and brushed Kent’s purple hair to the side. "You have become much taller, Kalimndra," she said, causing Kent to realize he was still in his demi-human form.
He quickly reverted to his human form, but even so, he stood 6’5" tall, three inches taller than her.

"Much better," she smiled beautifully, then apologized, "I am sorry for not being by your side until the very end, Kalimndra. Everything happened so fast that before I knew it, I was in this world with no way back to you. I really am sorry."
"No need to apologize for anything, big sister. I thought you were dead. Now that I have finally found you, I don’t care about anything else."
Hearing Kent’s reply, she smiled happily and nodded.
Then she began examining Kent’s body. After a few seconds of making sure he was alright, she asked the question on her mind...
"It is a long story, big sister."
"Tell me everything," she said, waving her hand. A sofa-like chair appeared for them to sit on. Naturally, she sat down, placed her head on Kent’s shoulder, and hugged his arm.
Kent, who wanted to use the excuse that the tribe leaders were waiting for him, had to abandon that thought, for he knew the kind of person his sister was.

Until she was satisfied, nobody else would get to have a moment with her baby brother. So he started to narrate everything that had happened after she was sucked into the portal and found herself here.

"After you left, which I thought meant you had died, I lost it and went berserk, killing as though that was my purpose in the universe. However, during that time, I also started to unlock the hidden abilities we had tried several times and failed to awaken.
Thanks to that, I managed to face the four Primordials and won. However, the last one managed to block the arrow I fired at his past self, and his present self came close to killing me.

But father stepped in and used his life to save mine." Kent sighed, thinking about the moment his father, who had always hated him, or so he thought, was taken down by a spear through the heart just so he could live on.

"He came through for me in the end, big sister. Because of that, we won. We celebrated the victory and mourned our losses. After that, I left our planet to travel to all the places we had planned to visit after the war.
After years of roaming, I returned home to bid farewell to the family before entering the cycle of reincarnation."

Fiannarel sighed and turned to look at Kent. "I knew father had been harsh on you, but deep down, he cared for you. In fact, I told him about your other identity a few weeks after I found out, but instead of making a fuss about it, he actually told me to keep an eye on you.
He was a good man and a great father. More importantly, he was also a great and brave warrior."
"That he was. I just hope he reincarnates too. I owe him an apology and a whole father-son bonding session."

Fiannarel chuckled. "As if reincarnation is that simple. Even as an Eternal, we haven’t figured out reincarnation yet. If it were that simple, I would have done it long ago and returned to the Infinity Universe.
It just happens without anyone controlling it. Sometimes the reincarnation is partial; sometimes, as with you, it is true, since you have your past-life memories. But nobody can navigate it."
Kent smiled and answered, "I figured it out a long time ago, big sister. In fact, I figured out the Origin of Life, Death, and Rebirth during the Primordial Era and have been using it for eras."
Fiannarel furrowed her brow and sat upright, looking back at the smug Kent. "What do you mean?"

Kent laughed and replied, "What I mean is that Kalimndra isn’t the only life I’ve lived. In fact, during the Primordial Era, I was known as the Primordial Chaos Dragon, Mom’s idol, and during the Divine Era, I was known as Lord Genesis, your idol.
It all started during the Primordial Era with a spell known as the Spell of Origin."

Fiannarel’s eyes widened as she looked at Kent with a dumbfounded expression. Never in the billions of years she had lived had she ever considered the possibility that her brother was someone she had idolized for years.
She had been infatuated with Lord Genesis to the point that whenever anything about him surfaced, she would do everything in her power either to acquire it or to get to the bottom of it.
That was how much she admired Lord Genesis. So to think he had been her little brother all along, she simply couldn’t wrap her mind around it.
After several minutes of processing what she had heard, a sigh escaped her lips.
"I guess that explains so many things. Perhaps it also explains why you are here."

chapters.title: Chapter 1775: The Invaluable Offer
paragraphs: Kent already knew the gist of what he was required to do before signing the contract with the Red Bone Chaos Tribe. However, hearing his sister say it made him finally understand the severity of everything.
Everyone was counting on him, so he knew he could not let them down. No matter what, he must rise to the occasion as he had done in the past.

"The seven tribe leaders have an offer for you. But before they say anything, I want to ask you something. How confident are you that you can master a technique, perhaps one so powerful that you would still need it even after becoming an Eternal one day?
I know you were a monster back during the Sun Era, but this is a different world altogether. So, how confident are you?"
Kent’s gaze narrowed as he heard his sister’s question. He took a deep breath, then sighed.
"I only needed a few seconds to learn Primordial-grade techniques, so maybe I will need about an hour or a day to master any technique you throw my way."
Fiannarel looked at Kent for a few seconds, then smirked.
"I guess we can go see them now. After all, if everything turns out in our favor in the end, we will have more time to catch up."
"That is true."

Kent took Fiannarel’s hand, and they started walking toward the building where the seven tribe leaders were waiting. If it were up to Fiannarel, they would all bring out their treasures and hand them over to Kent.
She trusted her brother, whom she had seen accomplish one incredible feat after another back in the Infinity Universe.
Now, learning that he was the legendary Lord Genesis, the father of all swordsmen, she believed he could achieve even more.
"Are you nervous?" she asked along the way, but Kent shook his head.

"Not really. I just don’t want to be stuck here for long. As much as I enjoy the life I am living here, the Infinity Universe is in danger, and my presence is required. So no matter what, I have to return home before it is too late."
Fiannarel nodded.

"Don’t worry. If you are anything like you were before, then I trust you will make it out. After all, you claim you had figured out reincarnation, so who is to say this isn’t all part of your big, elaborate plan?"
Kent chuckled.
"Let’s not blow things out of proportion, big sister. For all we know, I came here by accident."
"Somehow, I doubt that," Fiannarel laughed. Soon, they approached the building.

Kent, however, couldn’t help but wonder if all of this was merely one huge coincidence or just another event in his life that he had never known existed, like what happened when he absorbed the Blood Heart Seed he received from the Bloodvein Tribe.
Deep down, he doubted any of this was part of an elaborate plan orchestrated by the Spell of Origin. The thirteen soul fragments he had sent across space and time never made it here.
So naturally, the Spell of Origin clearly had no influence over this. That made him wonder once again if any of this had something to do with the Chaos Ascension King.
’Can’t be a coincidence, can it?’

They stepped into the hall, and at once, he felt seven terrifying gazes land on him. However, instead of feeling threatened, he seemed rather calm, almost unbothered that he was merely a Demigod standing before seven Eternals.
"Wow, tough crowd," he said jokingly, causing the seven tribe leaders to take deep breaths and reassess the brat standing before them.

He was no ordinary person, and they could finally see that. So they all changed their approach and, rather than seeing him as a brat, they chose to regard him as someone worthy of their trust and respect.
Jyoti Lata spoke.
"Kent Madson, these are the leaders of the other tribes in the Chaos Chasm. I invited them here following a discovery I made about the Chaos Ascension King Trial after I saw what you can do.
I don’t know if my deduction is correct, but I believe that to pass the Chaos Ascension King Trial, one must be able to harness the power of all seven tribes.
In other words, to pass the trial, you must learn all seven cultivation arts left behind by the Chaos Ascension King.
The other tribe leaders have agreed to give you their techniques, and so will I. Now, we just need to know if you can handle it.
We seven are all Eternals, yet none of us has mastered more than four levels of our respective cultivation arts, so you can only imagine how complex and demanding they are."
Parand took over.

"Also, to master all the techniques, you need to be exceptionally strong in body, soul, and mind. I have already witnessed you temper your body, and I have to say you are quite talented. However, how strong are your mind and soul?"
To answer their questions, Kent smiled and extended his soul, covering the entire space.
Then, in what could be considered the snap of a finger, the entire area was flooded with soul essence, so much so that all seven tribe leaders jumped to their feet.
Then their eyes widened when Kent spoke directly into their minds.
’Pretty strong, don’t you all think?’
"This..." Namarie tried to speak, but no words came out.
"Just how vast is your soul?" Zdzislav, the tribe chief who liked to flirt, asked.
"As vast as a universe, for lack of better words."
His soul had indeed become vast and boundless before coming here. However, after continuously leveling up and forming more cores, it had become even denser and far more powerful.
If he were still in the Infinity Universe, he would have tried creating more soul warriors. However, he could only wait until he returned.
Fiannarel smiled happily from the side, proud that her little brother had impressed the seven tribe leaders. This meant they could finally make headway.
"I don’t know how complex a cultivation technique that surpasses the Eternal realm can be, but I trust and believe in myself. I can master it in no time.
And before you call me arrogant, know that I have a record of mastering almost any technique in a less than thousandth of the time it would take the next prodigy.
So you can all rest assured that if what Tribe Leader Jyoti Lata said is indeed the case, your freedom will soon be yours."

They could no longer doubt his words, for he had already shocked them. While he could not even tickle their minds or souls, the mere fact that he could tap directly into their mental link and speak to them left them stunned.
They are Eternals, and he isn’t even a god yet.
Kent had proven himself to them, and with that, they were ready to hand over the most valuable treasure of their tribe.
"I will go first since I was the one who started all this," Jyoti Lata said, taking a step forward.
Kent took a deep breath and prepared himself for what was about to happen. If he had mastered all their techniques, perhaps returning home would already be within reach.

’I have only glimpsed the rank above the Sword Celestial stage, but instead of Primordial Essence, I saw Eternal Essence. If these techniques are anything like that, then I am about to experience the greatest moment of my life after thirteen reincarnations,’ he thought with a smile.
’Tower, are we set?’ he asked his assistant, and the response came immediately.
<We are good to go, Master.>

sentences.text: Kent already knew the gist of what he was required to do before signing the contract with the Red Bone Chaos Tribe.
However, hearing his sister say it made him finally understand the severity of everything.
Everyone was counting on him, so he knew he could not let them down.
No matter what, he must rise to the occasion as he had done in the past.
"The seven tribe leaders have an offer for you.
But before they say anything, I want to ask you something.
How confident are you that you can master a technique, perhaps one so powerful that you would still need it even after becoming an Eternal one day?
I know you were a monster back during the Sun Era, but this is a different world altogether.
So, how confident are you?"
Kent’s gaze narrowed as he heard his sister’s question.
He took a deep breath, then sighed.
"I only needed a few seconds to learn Primordial-grade techniques, so maybe I will need about an hour or a day to master any technique you throw my way."
Fiannarel looked at Kent for a few seconds, then smirked.
"I guess we can go see them now.
After all, if everything turns out in our favor in the end, we will have more time to catch up."
"That is true."
Kent took Fiannarel’s hand, and they started walking toward the building where the seven tribe leaders were waiting.
If it were up to Fiannarel, they would all bring out their treasures and hand them over to Kent.
She trusted her brother, whom she had seen accomplish one incredible feat after another back in the Infinity Universe.
Now, learning that he was the legendary Lord Genesis, the father of all swordsmen, she believed he could achieve even more.
"Are you nervous?" she asked along the way, but Kent shook his head.
"Not really.
I just don’t want to be stuck here for long.
As much as I enjoy the life I am living here, the Infinity Universe is in danger, and my presence is required.
So no matter what, I have to return home before it is too late."
Fiannarel nodded.
"Don’t worry.
If you are anything like you were before, then I trust you will make it out.
After all, you claim you had figured out reincarnation, so who is to say this isn’t all part of your big, elaborate plan?"
Kent chuckled.
"Let’s not blow things out of proportion, big sister.
For all we know, I came here by accident."
"Somehow, I doubt that," Fiannarel laughed.
Soon, they approached the building.

Kent, however, couldn’t help but wonder if all of this was merely one huge coincidence or just another event in his life that he had never known existed, like what happened when he absorbed the Blood Heart Seed he received from the Bloodvein Tribe.
Deep down, he doubted any of this was part of an elaborate plan orchestrated by the Spell of Origin.
The thirteen soul fragments he had sent across space and time never made it here.
So naturally, the Spell of Origin clearly had no influence over this.
That made him wonder once again if any of this had something to do with the Chaos Ascension King.
’Can’t be a coincidence, can it?’
They stepped into the hall, and at once, he felt seven terrifying gazes land on him.
However, instead of feeling threatened, he seemed rather calm, almost unbothered that he was merely a Demigod standing before seven Eternals.
"Wow, tough crowd," he said jokingly, causing the seven tribe leaders to take deep breaths and reassess the brat standing before them.
He was no ordinary person, and they could finally see that.
So they all changed their approach and, rather than seeing him as a brat, they chose to regard him as someone worthy of their trust and respect.
Jyoti Lata spoke.
"Kent Madson, these are the leaders of the other tribes in the Chaos Chasm.
I invited them here following a discovery I made about the Chaos Ascension King Trial after I saw what you can do.
I don’t know if my deduction is correct, but I believe that to pass the Chaos Ascension King Trial, one must be able to harness the power of all seven tribes.
In other words, to pass the trial, you must learn all seven cultivation arts left behind by the Chaos Ascension King.
The other tribe leaders have agreed to give you their techniques, and so will I.
Now, we just need to know if you can handle it.
We seven are all Eternals, yet none of us has mastered more than four levels of our respective cultivation arts, so you can only imagine how complex and demanding they are."
Parand took over.
"Also, to master all the techniques, you need to be exceptionally strong in body, soul, and mind.
I have already witnessed you temper your body, and I have to say you are quite talented.
However, how strong are your mind and soul?"
To answer their questions, Kent smiled and extended his soul, covering the entire space.
Then, in what could be considered the snap of a finger, the entire area was flooded with soul essence, so much so that all seven tribe leaders jumped to their feet.
Then their eyes widened when Kent spoke directly into their minds.
’Pretty strong, don’t you all think?’
"This..." Namarie tried to speak, but no words came out.
"Just how vast is your soul?" Zdzislav, the tribe chief who liked to flirt, asked.
"As vast as a universe, for lack of better words."
His soul had indeed become vast and boundless before coming here.
However, after continuously leveling up and forming more cores, it had become even denser and far more powerful.
If he were still in the Infinity Universe, he would have tried creating more soul warriors.
However, he could only wait until he returned.
Fiannarel smiled happily from the side, proud that her little brother had impressed the seven tribe leaders.
This meant they could finally make headway.
"I don’t know how complex a cultivation technique that surpasses the Eternal realm can be, but I trust and believe in myself.
I can master it in no time.
And before you call me arrogant, know that I have a record of mastering almost any technique in a less than thousandth of the time it would take the next prodigy.
So you can all rest assured that if what Tribe Leader Jyoti Lata said is indeed the case, your freedom will soon be yours."
They could no longer doubt his words, for he had already shocked them.
While he could not even tickle their minds or souls, the mere fact that he could tap directly into their mental link and speak to them left them stunned.
They are Eternals, and he isn’t even a god yet.
Kent had proven himself to them, and with that, they were ready to hand over the most valuable treasure of their tribe.
"I will go first since I was the one who started all this," Jyoti Lata said, taking a step forward.
Kent took a deep breath and prepared himself for what was about to happen.
If he had mastered all their techniques, perhaps returning home would already be within reach.
’I have only glimpsed the rank above the Sword Celestial stage, but instead of Primordial Essence, I saw Eternal Essence.
If these techniques are anything like that, then I am about to experience the greatest moment of my life after thirteen reincarnations,’ he thought with a smile.
’Tower, are we set?’ he asked his assistant, and the response came immediately.
<We are good to go, Master.>

chapters.title: Chapter 1776: The Seven Chaos Cultivation Arts
paragraphs: The moment Jyoti Lata stopped before Kent, she extended her finger toward his forehead and spoke, "Open your mind and soul to whatever I will be transmitting. Do not resist, and most importantly, do not access it until I am done transmitting it."
Kent nodded and opened his soul. "I am ready."
She nodded, then said something brief about the technique she was about to transmit.
"The Cultivation Art left for the Red Bone Chaos Tribe is called the Red Bone Chaos Devouring Art. As its name suggests, it has to do with devouring and refining anything that contains Chaos Essence.

Depending on how much you’ve mastered it, you can devour several billion years’ worth of energy in mere seconds. Meaning, in battle, if your comprehension is deep enough, you can devour, refine, and replenish your strength and energy without much of a struggle.
Basically, anything that contains Chaos Essence can be devoured, all the way to Laws and Daos. Even Origin Essence and Eternal Laws cannot be excluded."

"Sounds like it is a one-of-a-kind technique, perfect for someone like me who always has powerful enemies," he laughed and said. "In that case, I am more than eager to see what this Red Bone Chaos Devouring Art can do."
"Very well." She pressed her finger against Kent’s forehead, then, after taking a deep breath, began to transmit the technique.
The moment she began, messages started to appear before Kent...
<You are receiving a Limitless Grade Cultivation Technique called the Red Bone Chaos Devouring Art>
<Progress: 2%>
’Limitless, huh?’ A smile appeared on his face.
The progress continued to climb, perhaps much faster than Jyoti Lata had expected, considering the shocked expression on her beautiful face.
However, it soon turned into a smile. ’This kid is a monster among monsters.’
The other Eternals who sensed what was happening also came to the same conclusion. Normally, it takes the average person between 100 and 1,000 years to receive any of the cultivation arts.
However, from the look of things, Kent would soon finish receiving the technique in less than 10 minutes.
"As expected of my baby brother, he sure is full of surprises," Fiannarel smiled beautifully, proud to have someone like Kent as her baby brother.
Within 4 minutes, progress reached 95%, and in no time, the final message appeared.
<You have successfully received the Red Bone Chaos Devouring Art>
"Well, that was quick," Kent said, a smug expression appearing on his face.
Jyoti Lata looked at him with a stunned expression for a whole minute before shaking her head. "Unbelievable. At this rate, you can even receive all techniques before learning them."
Kent smiled and was about to say, ’I bet I can learn it in less than an hour,’ when the Tower spoke...

<The master cannot learn the technique yet. For reasons I cannot explain yet, the master must first awaken the third Blood Gate, form the third Chaos Heart, and cultivate the third Demon Body. Trust me, this will benefit you more than you think.>
’I trust you, Tower.’
He lifted his head and looked at Jyoti Lata. "In any case, I don’t plan on learning any of the techniques yet since I still have to form my third Chaos Heart and the third Demon Body."
"Very well, then I will go next," Borislav, the Tribe Leader of the Void Vein Chaos Tribe, said and walked forward while Jyoti Lata walked back and sat down.
"A little something you should know about the Void Vein Chaos Scripture is that it allows you to harness the absolute power of the Void by connecting to Void Veins or creating your own.
To master it, you must form or connect to at least two Void Veins. Once that is accomplished, the rest will be up to you and how much you can harness the true power of the Void Chaos."
He reached forward and started to transmit the technique.
In all of the Chaos Chasm, his tribe is an expert in stealth and manipulation. They can manipulate the Void to the point that if they don’t want you to catch them, you cannot.
Their power is that great, and now Kent is receiving it.
About the same time it took Jyoti Lata, the transmission ended, and the third Tribe Leader approached Kent while Borislav walked back to his seat, shaking his head with a smile on his face.

Tribe Leader Veylan Seren smiled and said, "The Obsidian Chaos Dragon Physique is the best body tempering, forging, and refining technique you would ever encounter. In fact, I am glad you are a dragon and are also cultivating the Nine Demon Body Tempering Art."
He laughed, causing the other three leaders to curse him deeply, knowing that when it comes to physical strength, the Obsidian Scale Chaos Tribe stands at the top.
While the Red Bone Chaos Tribe is also known for body tempering, their power comes from devouring, whereas the Obsidian Scale Chaos Tribe specializes in true body tempering.
So, to Kent, his laughter made Veylan Seren appear carefree. To the rest of the Eternals, he was mocking them.
"You are going to forge your body into a living weapon, each claw becoming a weapon that can cut through Laws, Daos, and everything it touches.

In fact, now that you have received the Red Bone Chaos Devouring Art, cultivating the Obsidian Chaos Dragon Physique will be much easier. After all, what better way to temper the body than with devoured energy?"
"Lucky me, I guess," Kent laughed, and Veylan Seren laughed with him.
Afterward, he spent 5 minutes transferring the technique to him...
"Remember, kid, if you manage to free us, I will personally spend a million years forging you into a weapon so lethal that even Universe Lords would cower before you."
Veylan Seren said, his aura spreading through the air.
Kent nodded and replied, "I doubt it would take a million years, but I will take you up on that offer."
"Hahahaha, I like your sense of humor, kid. Good, this will make everything simple then," he laughed one last time before walking back to his seat.

"You know, when Fiannarel said you are someone who can see and attack both the past and the future, I had my doubts. However, now, I think you might just be the first person in the history of this world who can master the Essence of Existence."
Tribe Leader Zdzislav stated, causing the other Tribe Leaders to furrow their brows.
"Surely, you must be exaggerating here, Zdzislav," Tumenk, the leader of the Celestial Abyss Chaos Tribe, questioned.
Zdzislav, the leader of the Astral Eye Chaos Tribe, smiled and shook his head.

"I don’t know how he managed it, but rooted deep within his subconscious is the Root of Existence. If he can awaken it and let it bloom into an All-Seeing Chaos Existence Tree, then perhaps he would accomplish what the best of us couldn’t."
"This..."
The Tribe Leaders, and even Fiannarel, who knew just how big a deal the Essence of Existence was, looked at Kent in shock.
Sensing their gazes, Kent flipped his hair to the side and puffed his chest out. "Never underestimate the power of a Chaos Dragon."
The ladies in the hall rolled their eyes while Veylan Seren exploded into resounding laughter.
