chapters.title: Chapter 1786: Overpowered Techniques (7)
paragraphs: "You know, if I am indeed the Chaos Ascension King, then I guess it is a bit humbling to know I lost to the Paragon, whom, while I don’t like to brag, I saved not long ago," Kent said, flicking his hair back as he stared at Lady Kenzie and the Death dude.
Leaving the Eternals to ponder his words, he focused on the Death dude.

When he started cultivating the World Root Chaos Scripture, he sensed a call from deep within his soul, far beneath the Blood Sea. Initially, he was mistaken about where it came from, but it sounded again.
Focusing his mind there, he began to investigate.

The last thing he wanted was to release something he shouldn’t, especially now that the Underworld Soul River seemed to be undergoing an upgrade. Something might have slipped through during that time.
So he moved cautiously, and during his investigation, he discovered a figure chained deep within the vast, expansive blood sea of his soul.
He wasn’t malnourished or suffering. If anything, the only inconvenience Kent saw was the chains binding him. It appears someone had chained him, and Kent seems to know who...
Kent questioned him:

"I wonder why you are here without my knowledge. But I am going to be curious and ask, what the hell are you doing inside my soul, buddy?" The question was simple, but the fury in the figure’s eyes was simply overwhelming.
He looked back at Kent and gritted his teeth.

"I have never been humiliated like this before, Dragon. In all my existence, the only person who dared look down on me was the Chaos Ascension King, but even he had to attest to the fact that I am someone equal to him in both greatness and finesse.
So to be chained here inside this lowly place, I have to be honest, I am very angry and would probably claim your life as compensation."
Kent furrowed his brow and asked, "So you know the Chaos Ascension King?"
"Of course I do. He and I go way back, Dragon. You had better release me and beg for my forgiveness. Maybe I will have mercy and only turn you into my Death Puppet."
Kent laughed, intrigued despite knowing he stood in the presence of Death.

"I have to ask, though, if someone of your caliber, someone who once stood shoulder to shoulder with the Chaos Ascension King, ends up chained inside my soul, then what do you make of the fact that maybe I am far more powerful than you think?"
At Kent’s question, a grin formed on the man’s face, and he answered,
"It would do you good to find out whether you are brave enough to loosen these chains a bit."
"No, don’t do it, Master. He would kill you before you could even breathe," Lady Kenzie appeared beside Kent, narrowing her gem-like green eyes at the chained figure.
"Of course I know that. I am not stupid," Kent replied, regarding Lady Kenzie for a few seconds before turning back to the Death dude, who now held a hateful gaze toward her.
"Life, you seem much weaker than I expected. Why? Did you fail to live on as you should?"

Lady Kenzie smirked. "Says Death, who lost to Master’s will. Or do you think Master wouldn’t know you would rebel and make plans for you?" She sneered and added, "In fact, I never expected you to still be sane after all these years had passed."

Death chuckled, looking pissed and nonchalant at the same time. "Existence is an anagram of Life. We never truly know what lies ahead, aside from that Paragon bastard. But when you give life to Death, you don’t expect it to abide by your rules anymore, do you?"
Lady Kenzie sighed and nodded. "I do. However, you have to know that the Master gave us this existence, and for that, we should be grateful."
"I guess you are right." Death nodded and looked at Kent, "However, he is not the Master. He is not the Chaos Ascension King, so don’t expect me to bow to him."
At his words, Kent smiled. "Regardless of who I am or who I am not, the question now is whether or not you will abide by the will of the Chaos Ascension King and submit to my rule."
Kent said the words casually, then chuckled. However, the next second, his entire soul sea shook, and Death was sent to his knees.
RUMBLE! RUMBLE!
The crimson clouds parted, and the blood-red sea divided, revealing a terrifying eye so powerful that when Kent looked into it, cracks formed across his soul.
"All hail the Sovereign of Life and Death," Lady Kenzie said as she dropped to her knees.
To Kent’s shock, Death did the same. "All hail the Sovereign of Life and Death."

No sound followed, but when the eye closed, and the sky returned to normal, Kent sensed a shift in the air. He turned his attention back to Death only to see him still kneeling, the chains that had bound him now gone.
"Well, well, well, look how the mighty have fallen," Kent said.
But instead of being angry, Death raised his head and smiled at Kent.
"I never expected you to possess the power to invoke the will of the Chaos Ascension King. If I had known, I wouldn’t have threatened you."
Kent raised a brow and replied, "Oh, that? I merely joked about that. Who knew it would have...?"
"This..." Death was at a loss for words.
"Relax. I am sure whoever you are or were wouldn’t change. However, you are bound to me now, so maybe let’s get along. Hopefully, when we meet the Chaos Ascension King, we can both get what we want."
"And what is it that you want?" Death asked.
"To go back home to my loved ones. They miss me, and I miss them."

Death stood there for a few seconds before nodding. "Very well, Dragon. We can both get what we want if we cooperate, so I will cooperate with you. Just don’t take too long. My patience can only last for a few million years."
"That is more than enough for me to reach the stage where I wouldn’t need you anymore."
Kent grinned, looking back at Death. "How does it feel to finally be free?"
Death narrowed his eyes and said, "I don’t know if you are indeed the Chaos Ascension King, but stop wasting time and get on with your cultivation. Death has no time to waste."
Kent grinned and snapped his fingers, sending both Lady Kenzie and Death away.
"What an uptight buddy. When I surpass the Chaos Ascension King, I will be sure to tell him a piece of my mind."
Kent chuckled, turning back to Namarie, who was now on her feet.

"I don’t know why you have decided not to cultivate Death, but know this: both Life and Death are supposed to go hand in hand. So think about it, and if you must, make sure you and your people start cultivating it."
"I will heed your advice, Lord Kent."
Kent nodded, not minding how Namarie now referred to him. She might be an Eternal, but before the Sovereign of Life and Death, she knew she could not look down on him.
He turned to the next cultivation art he would comprehend.
’Up next, the Primordial Abyss Chaos Heart Art.’

Just don’t take too long.
My patience can only last for a few million years."
"That is more than enough for me to reach the stage where I wouldn’t need you anymore."
Kent grinned, looking back at Death.
"How does it feel to finally be free?"
Death narrowed his eyes and said, "I don’t know if you are indeed the Chaos Ascension King, but stop wasting time and get on with your cultivation.
Death has no time to waste."
Kent grinned and snapped his fingers, sending both Lady Kenzie and Death away.
"What an uptight buddy.
When I surpass the Chaos Ascension King, I will be sure to tell him a piece of my mind."
Kent chuckled, turning back to Namarie, who was now on her feet.
"I don’t know why you have decided not to cultivate Death, but know this: both Life and Death are supposed to go hand in hand.
So think about it, and if you must, make sure you and your people start cultivating it."
"I will heed your advice, Lord Kent."
Kent nodded, not minding how Namarie now referred to him.
She might be an Eternal, but before the Sovereign of Life and Death, she knew she could not look down on him.
He turned to the next cultivation art he would comprehend.
’Up next, the Primordial Abyss Chaos Heart Art.’

chapters.title: Chapter 1787: Overpowered Techniques (8)
paragraphs: "He is about to cultivate the Primordial Abyss Chaos Heart Art," Tumenk, the leader of the Primordial Abyss Chaos Tribe, said, a smile appearing on his face.

It had been a while since something had excited powerful beings such as the seven gathered here. However, now, watching Kent create one miracle after another, they couldn’t help but look forward to what he would accomplish next.
Of course, Tumenk wanted to see what Kent would achieve with the Primordial Abyss Chaos Heart Art. Unlike the other techniques, this one was meant to strengthen, expand, and evolve the Chaos Heart.

His tribe was the strongest simply because of their robust Chaos Hearts and boundless energy. They had more energy to pour into their attacks, making them much more likely to outlast their opponents and win battles.
Now, Kent had begun cultivating it.
"I expect great things, kid," he muttered and began to wait.
Meanwhile, Kent found himself in the middle of a storm. He stood atop a mountain that hung just beneath the storm clouds.
"Holy mother of—"
Before he could finish his words, a deadly bolt tore through the storm clouds and struck his chest, sending him crashing onto his butt.
For a moment, his vision turned blurry, and he could swear he saw his wives reaching for his hand. However, the next second, messages appeared, causing his eyes to widen.
<You have absorbed a large amount of Chaos Essence>

<Welcome to the Grim Star Chaos Storm. You will be bombarded with Chaos-infused lightning endlessly. The more you absorb, the stronger your Chaos Heart becomes. Endure the first Star Bombardment to evolve your Chaos Heart to the First Star Cycle.
Endure the second, and the cycle continues until you can’t endure anymore or have completed all Seven Star Cycles before you can proceed to the next stage.>
RUMBLE!

Another lightning bolt tore through the clouds, and just like before, it struck his chest, causing Kent to scream in pain. He endured, but the merciless storm and lightning hadn’t even begun their true bombardment yet.
In fact, the power behind the attacks seemed to increase with every bolt he endured.
’At this rate, I will have to tap out in a couple of hours,’ Kent thought to himself.
Yet a week later, he remained where he was, his body crawling with lightning.
’I am still here, I guess.’
He smiled and welcomed more torture.
On the outside, no new changes occurred even after a month had passed since he began cultivating the Primordial Abyss Chaos Heart Art.
The first few weeks had been eventful for the seven leaders. They kept discussing the achievements Kent had so easily accumulated over the past couple of years.
However, as time passed and no new changes occurred, they started to grow worried, especially Tumenk, whose cultivation method Kent had begun.
Perhaps because Kent always seemed to create a miracle whenever he cultivated one of the other techniques, they had all been looking forward to seeing him do it again this time as well.
However, even after two months without any signs of progress, they began to wonder whether something had happened to him.

"Relax, everyone. The mere fact that he hasn’t come out yet shows he has perhaps encountered something extraordinary, and it is taking some time to handle it," Fiannarel said, calming them down a bit.
Of course, she was also worried, but she knew Kent wasn’t as simple as one would think, so she didn’t let her concern show on her face like the others did.
Three months soon passed, but nothing else changed.
Now, they were genuinely worried.

Seven months later, they all jumped to their feet, their expressions narrowing as they looked at Kent, who now had a faint aura surrounding him. Tumenk, in particular, unconsciously stepped forward, almost as if he couldn’t see clearly from where he stood.

For a few minutes, nothing else happened. However, just when they were about to sigh and attribute everything to their imagination, a powerful explosion of energy erupted from Kent’s body, and then...
BUZZZZZ!

A circular diagram made of golden metallic materialized behind Kent, and seven white Star Orbs hung within the ring, oozing such overwhelming power that Tumenk instinctively shielded himself, and the others did the same.
But things didn’t end there.
Just when the first ring appeared, the second also buzzed into existence, much larger than the first, yet also containing seven Star Orbs within it.
BUZZZ!
The third appeared, circling around both the first and second rings, creating a three-layered cultivation diagram that left Tumenk and everyone else looking pale.
"This can’t actually be the infamous Seven-Star Cycle Evolution Diagram, right?" Parand asked, looking back at Tumenk, who seemed pale beyond measure.
He was excited, stunned, and, most importantly, conflicted.
His conflict wasn’t that he didn’t know what to do about Kent. It was more like he couldn’t tell whether Kent was indeed the reincarnation of the Chaos Ascension King.

It had merely been a thought at first, but as time passed and Kent kept accomplishing one mind-bending feat after another, the thought that he might actually be the Chaos Ascension King started to take root in their minds.
Now, he had done it again, and so Tumenk was torn on what to do.
"Tumenk, is this really the Seven-Star Cycle Evolution Diagram?"

Tumenk turned and looked at the other Eternals before nodding. He then summoned his own Star Cycle Evolution Diagram, but it had only one layer with five yellow Star Orbs, unlike the white ones behind Kent.
More importantly, Tumenk’s single diagram possessed far more power than all three of Kent’s combined.
"He has, without a doubt, awakened the Grim Star Chaos Storm and endured seven agonizing Star Cycles... no, twenty-one Star Cycles, considering he has three Chaos Hearts.

"You have to understand that before one can begin Abyss Tempering, one must first evolve the Chaos Heart through what we call Star Cycle Evolution. At the first stage of the Primordial Abyss Chaos Heart Art, each completed Star Cycle makes the Chaos Heart ten times stronger and larger.

"This means I have attained a fiftyfold expansion after completing the Five-Star Cycle Evolution. This kid, however, has completed twenty-one Star Cycles, meaning each of his three Chaos Hearts are now each seventy times larger and stronger than before."

"But to fully cultivate the first form of the Primordial Abyss Chaos Heart Art, he must firmly connect all three Chaos Hearts to the Abyss, thereby forming the Seed of the Abyss. It is that seed which will continuously empower his Chaos Hearts with the Abyss itself, allowing him to wield the most dreadful form of Chaos Energy—the Abyssal Chaos Energy."
The seven tribe leaders and Fiannarel looked at Kent, and for a moment, they wondered whether giving him their cultivation techniques had truly been the right decision.

After all, where Kent came from, the most powerful beings were the Primordials. However, if what these seven techniques were turning him into was any indication, then by the time he attained godhood, not even a Celestial would survive a single attack from him.
This begged the question... what was he training for?
More importantly, was this fate at work, or was it all Kent’s own doing?
Those questions remained unanswered for now.
But one thing was certain.
Kent wasn’t here by accident.
And whatever he had come here to accomplish, when he returned to his own universe, the answer would become clear to him.

chapters.title: Chapter 1788: Overpowered Techniques (9)
paragraphs: Kent slowly opened his eyes, his Chaos Aura now filled with Abyssal Qi, the kind that had prevented Sanders, the Bone Lich Undead Emperor, from saving his parents from the Abyssal Chaos many years ago.
Now, in less than a year, Kent had comprehended it and even merged it with his Chaos Heart, allowing him to harness the most potent form of his Chaos Qi—Abyssal Chaos Qi.
With all three cores each undergoing Seven Star Cycle Evolutions, he could now be considered done with the first form of the Primordial Abyss Chaos Heart Art, and he could move on to the next one.
But before that, Kent first tested something...

He opened his palm and summoned Gaap. Then, tapping into his first Chaos Heart, he summoned 5% of the Abyssal Chaos Qi and laced it around the sword. Then, tapping into his Extreme Sword Energy, he imbued the sword with 5% of it and stood up.

He walked a few kilometers and stopped before a mountain. After making sure the mountain was empty, he casually swung the sword at it, and a thin line of Abyssal Chaos infused with both Sword Intent and Sword Aura flashed out and disappeared.
The next second, the mountain was severed diagonally in half, one part sliding off. But that wasn’t what Kent was aiming at.
His gaze followed the clouds that had parted, revealing the dark expanse of space. Several hundred thousand kilometers away, an asteroid large enough to decimate an entire city was severed in half.
Kent lowered his sword and smiled. "I suppose if I don’t want to kill anyone at the sword competition, I have to find a way to limit myself."
<The master used Abyssal Chaos alongside his Sword Energy. Perhaps just the Sword Energy would do.>
Kent smiled and unsummoned Gaap, causing it to return to his Soul Sea before replying to Tower...
’That may be true in some way, considering I will be fighting sword geniuses. However, do you seriously think they can handle 5% of my Sword Energy if they are below the Sword God Stage?’
He shook his head, then teleported back to the space where he had been cultivating and sat in a lotus posture.
’I think we should start making plans to go on the offensive when I return. I think attacking the other races that once attacked the universe would help me understand my current capabilities.’
<I understand, Master. I believe when I merge back with the other part in the Infinity Universe, we will finally be able to come to terms with what the Black Dungeon is and how to conquer it.>
’Very well. For now, let’s handle the 6th technique.’
Kent sighed and jumped into the next technique, the Heaven Splitting Chaos Wings...

This time, he appeared on a glassy path leading to a temple, or maybe a castle, or just an ordinary building built from obsidian jade. The structure stood tall and imposing, almost as if it were home to dread.
Looking at the thick walls, Kent couldn’t help but wonder if this building and the Blood Temple of the Soul Temple shared some similarities.
’Quite ironic how the word "temple" seems to be in almost everything vile and dangerous around me,’ he smiled, and then he pushed the fleeting thought to the back of his mind.
The last thing he wanted was to make the same mistake he had made in the past when he chose to spare the life of the Blood Ancestor.
The last time they met before Jest went into the final battle against the Foreign Race, he had possessed the power to kill him.
However, for reasons he couldn’t help but scoff at at the moment, Kent just knew he had made a mistake, or maybe he hadn’t.
Regardless, he was here now, so he could only focus on what lay ahead.

His footsteps echoed across the glassy floor, soon reaching the giant gate leading into the building. The gates were already open, so when he stood before them, he could see the inside of the building.
Kent stopped in his tracks and lifted his head, staring at what could be considered the most wondrous sight.

A stone tablet, towering and beautiful, stood at the center of the building, engraved with ancient runes. At a glance, he counted only 100 runes, but each rune held so much meaning that his mind nearly collapsed trying to comprehend them all at once.
’That was dangerous...’ Kent said inwardly and winced. Then he looked up, beyond the tablet.

His gaze fell on a beautiful metallic wing, its features made of piercing metal, each feather holding so much power that his mind scrambled under the sheer amount of information he was receiving just by staring at it.
It was red and black, and, more importantly, it came in seven pairs, each pair longer and more imposing than the last.
The moment Kent beheld the name written beneath these seven pairs of wings, his body on the outside trembled, and the Jade Void Wing appeared.
"Here hangs the complete form of the Heaven Splitting Jade Void Wing."

Kent’s consciousness, standing at the building’s entrance, was soon lifted into the air by an invincible force, drawing him closer to the wings. When he was only two meters away, his blood essence was extracted, and it merged with the wing...

On the outside, the Heaven Splitting Jade Void Wing manifested behind him, the space around him shaking as void cracks started to snake around him, almost as if reality was struggling to contain the power of the wing.
Parand stood up, her expression filled with delight as she gazed at the awakening of the Heaven Splitting Jade Void Wing.
For three full hours, the awakening continued. Finally, when it settled, thin red runes started to emerge from the Heaven Splitting Jade Void Wing and spread outward from Kent...
It took Parand ten full minutes to understand what was happening. After all, she had never expected to meet someone who commanded the Heaven Splitting Jade Void Wing.
In her billions of years of existence, she had read many records, but the records of the wings said to be able to harness the power of the Void Chaos had never explained how they could do that.
They only stated that as one comprehended the Void, so too would they be able to move. The more they understood about the Void, the faster they could move using the Heaven Splitting Jade Void Wing...
"I believe he is comprehending the Void and building his Void Storm Domain," Parand said with a delighted expression.
Right now, the red runes seemed to have started to spread far and wide, already covering a radius of over one kilometer...
"A little context, Parand," Zdzislav asked, and Parand, who was overcome with joy, smiled and added,

"The Void Storm Domain is basically the speed range of the wings. Take, for example, my Flame Storm Domain. It covers 10,000,000 light-years. This means that at any moment, I can move and appear anywhere within those 10,000,000 light-years.
I achieved that by comprehending the Six Wing Laws—well, I have completed only four, but you get the gist."
"So how vast was your Flame Storm Domain when you comprehended the first Wing Law?" Fiannarel asked.
"I was only a Supreme then, but it was 10,000 light-years." She looked at Kent, whose Void Storm Domain had already reached ten kilometers in radius in less than ten minutes...
"I wonder how vast his domain will be after comprehending the Law of Ascension of the Void Storm."

chapters.title: Chapter 1789: Overpowered Techniques (10)
paragraphs: "Well, I suppose his comprehension speed is indeed very monstrous," Parand muttered, looking at the vast Void Storm Domain now covering a radius of 100,000 kilometers after just a day of Kent cultivating it.
The other Tribe Leaders, while they didn’t know much about the Heaven Splitting Chaos Wings Art, could tell that what Kent had achieved was far beyond normal.
The mere fact that he had already reached a radius of 100,000 kilometers was more than enough for many Demigods at his level to spend over a year achieving the same thing he had done in a single day.
But things didn’t end there. Ten days later, his Void Storm Domain had reached 1,000,000 kilometers, and by the end of the first month, it had already expanded to one light-year.

They could only sit back and watch him progress faster than anyone at his level should. Thankfully, while they would have loved nothing more than to watch his domain continue expanding, they knew he had a limit, and that limit came a year later.
But by then, his domain had already reached 120,000 light-years.
Kent opened his eyes and jumped to his feet, tapping into the Void Storm Domain. His Heaven Splitting Jade Void Wings flapped, and he vanished from sight, appearing several billion kilometers away.
"WOW, that isn’t normal, right?" he asked, and was about to move again when a terrifying shockwave slammed into his body.
He had never expected it, but even if he had, the shockwave was so powerful that he lost his balance. However, before he could be swept away, Parand caught him.
Kent found himself standing before her, almost as if she hadn’t moved even a finger.
Naturally, she hadn’t moved her body. She had merely reached forward with her left hand and caught him. However, in reality, that casual movement had traveled several billion kilometers.
Parand smiled, almost as if she had read Kent’s mind, and said,

"Think of your domain as an extension of your body. Right now, it is vast and expansive, but if you can harness its power as your own, then naturally, you can stand here and attack someone several light-years away from you."
Kent nodded, then closed his eyes and took a deep breath. He activated the Void Storm Domain and, just as Parand had said, imagined himself becoming the domain and the domain becoming him.
For a moment, his body trembled as he felt himself begin to expand. In no time, he felt as though he were as vast as 120,000 light-years... if that even made sense.
He could see everything around him, his vision expanding as his body grew. ’This is just mind-bending,’ he said inwardly, but thanks to his vast Soul Sea, he felt no discomfort.
Parand smiled, seeing how easily Kent had grasped the concept of becoming one with his domain.
"Now, reach forward and pick a fruit from the tree 40,000 light-years due east of you."
Kent nodded, then focused on the tree. His hand moved, and the next second, a green fruit lay in his palm.
"Wow, this is too overpowered."
Parand laughed, seeing how happy and shocked Kent was after experiencing only the tip of the iceberg. For now, she allowed him to experience things for himself.
After all, he still had one more technique to learn, so all the tutoring they had planned for him would have to wait.
Kent seemed to understand that as well, so after picking a few fruits for Fiannarel and the Tribe Leaders, he returned to his cultivation.

’Whatever I am here training for, it better be something worth my time.’
He laughed, then focused on the final technique... the Heavenly Chaos Eye Canon...

The moment he tapped into the Heavenly Chaos Eye Canon technique, he appeared in a completely dark space. Everything about the place reeked of danger, but for reasons Kent had no idea of, he knew he was about to experience the biggest breakthrough of his life.
He sat in a lotus posture and closed his eyes. Well, that was what the technique told him to do, so he did, and a few minutes later, streams of golden runes started appearing in the air.
However, just as they appeared, they began to move and entered his forehead.
On the outside, a vertical eye tattoo appeared on Kent’s forehead. Then, from within it, a diagram made of red metal appeared above his head.
Suddenly, a faint grey eye started to form within the diagram.

Zdzislav smiled and clapped his hands. "What an interesting kid. I guess now we can truly say he is the Chaos Ascension King. After all, he has awakened the Eye of Chaos, the most dreadful eye said to have beheld Existence in its entirety."
The other Tribe Chiefs felt their bodies tremble with joy. Even if they turned out to be wrong, they still wouldn’t mind calling Kent their Young Lord.
After all, he had accomplished what none of them could, not even their ancestors.
A year later, a majestic red eye lined with hints of gold, purple, and silver hovered behind Kent, giving him a presence that commanded respect.
[Infinity Universe - Blood Temple]
A woman with flowing red hair and a voluptuous body, seated in a pool of blood, suddenly snapped her eyes open, blood seeping from the corners of both eyes.
Her expression had become pale, so pale that she fell backward and slammed into the edge of the pool. Luckily, she wasn’t easily intimidated, so she managed to calm her racing heart.
"Eye of Chaos... but how," she muttered, looking dazed.
Just now, she had felt a powerful pressure coming from somewhere far away, perhaps too far away for her Eyes of Blood to see. However, she had felt it, and it had terrified her.

Unfortunately for her, she recognized what kind of eye it was. The Eye of Chaos was one of the Seven Primal Eyes. Aside from it, there were the Eyes of Fate, Purgatory, Destiny, Karma, Life, and Death.
From the records passed down through time, the Eye of Chaos was wielded by an existence that sought to rise above Existence itself.
When she started cultivating the Eye of Blood, she learned that while it was possible to see beyond what was and gaze upon what could be, the path to that was impossible.
The records spoke of the day the Eye of Chaos gazed upon Existence. It was said that everything known and long forgotten trembled as it witnessed Existence seeing itself.
The wielder of the Eye of Chaos had bitten off more than they could chew. In the end, they were forced to destroy their own eyes, blinding themselves to the truth, never to see it again.
"But why... how? How can the Eye of Chaos appear again, and in such dangerous times?"
She rose from the pool of blood, and an elegant red dress wrapped itself around her.
She walked out of her mansion and stood atop one of the tallest mountains in the Celestial Realm.
"Has the Chaos Ascension King returned, or is this just fate playing its games on me?" She looked up, almost as if trying to meet someone’s gaze.
Naturally, far within the Primordial Chaos, hidden deep in the Void, a woman seated in a lotus posture opened her blood-red eyes and gazed back at her.
Seeing the blank expression on her face, the Blood Empress sighed and called out,
"Blood Ancestor, send word to the Celestial Supreme. I want to have a word with him."

chapters.title: Chapter 1790: Chaos Ascension King Trial
paragraphs: [50 Years Later]
Kent slowly opened his eyes, his body releasing waves of Chaos Qi so intense that he seemed to bend the space around him with a mere touch.
It had been 50 years since he began cultivating in the Red Bone Chaos Tribe.

Within the first 30 years, during which he cultivated the seven cultivation arts given to him by the seven tribe leaders, he had accomplished so much. However, he went on to do more during the remaining 20 years.

First, he decided to handle his cores. After performing the 21 Star Cycle Evolution on his three Chaos Hearts, Kent decided to try something mad. Instead of merely tempering his Chaos Heart, he used the technique on his other cores.
The idea was crazy, something Tumenk warned him against. However, he merely smiled and went ahead to do it anyway, and he succeeded.

Not only did he complete the 21 Star Cycle Evolution on his Chaos Hearts, but he also completed the 21 Star Cycle Evolution on his Blood Core, Evil Core, Ice Core, Flame Core, Lightning Core, Void Core, and lastly, Abyssal Core.

He formed the Abyssal Core since he could, and now he has an affinity for it. He didn’t want to leave space inside his Blood Gates, so he formed it by using the connection he shared with it through the Primordial Abyss Chaos Heart Art.
But that wasn’t all he did in the past 20 years.
While proceeding from the Undying Obsidian Body to the Undying Golden Body wasn’t an option, since he had limited time, Kent focused rather on cultivating more of the Nine Demon Body Tempering Art.

He gave himself five years to cultivate at least seven bodies. Safe to say, he failed, but he cultivated up to five bodies. This boosted his strength several times beyond what he could previously harness.
He also expanded his Void Storm Domain from 120,000 light-years to 500,000 light-years. Kent had no idea why he would need that much speed this early in his journey.
After all, even as gods, moving that fast was impractical. In fact, not many could handle that speed.
However, when his mind went back to his past lives, where, during many of the battles he fought, he had been too late to save his friends and allies, he wished he could expand his domain even more.
When the threat arrived, it would cover many worlds, and the ability to be anywhere with a mere flap of his wings would surely come in handy.

Because of that, he went ahead and cultivated his bones to the Primordial Origin Bones stage, leaving him with only the Eternal Devouring Bones and Chaos Ascension Emperor Bones to go before he would fully complete the first form of the Red Bone Chaos Devouring Art.
As for his Eye of Chaos, Kent had unlocked some abilities and even managed to merge his Omniscient Jade Eyes with it.
But the moment he did that, the next couple of evolutions of the Omniscient Jade Eyes were triggered, and before he knew it, he had attained the Omniscient Dao Eyes.

Now, he could see much deeper into the past and further into the future, depending on how strong the target’s soul was. He had done so much that even he had lost track of how much stronger he had become.
However, one thing was certain: he had become powerful, so powerful, in fact, that he could finally return to the Infinity Universe without fear, even if he met the Blood Ancestor again.
His hair had grown longer, and even he seemed much taller in both his human and demi-human forms. As for his dragon form, he had finally reached 1 km in length...
Kent rose to his feet and turned toward the seven tribe leaders and Fiannarel, who had come to congratulate him.
They had all witnessed the achievements he had achieved over the last 50 years, so mere words weren’t enough to convey the joy they all felt for his success.
"Well then, I guess what is left now is the Chaos Ascension King Trial," Kent said after accepting their congratulations.
"It appears so," Parand said, a smile forming on her face.
Kent also smiled and said, "Honestly, even if I somehow manage to pass the trial and free you all, there is a high chance you will be suppressed when you appear in my universe.

As I have already said, the strongest in my world are Primordials, but even they are not allowed to fight in the open. They can only fight in the void since a mere clap of their hands against one another can destroy planets.
That said, there might even be a case where you all would be denied entry. What then do you plan to do if that is the case?"

The seven tribe leaders smiled at Kent’s words. They had, of course, thought of all these things many times already, but at every turn, they didn’t mind being suppressed. As long as they could step out of this place, they would very much enjoy the freedom they would be given.
As for the scenario where they couldn’t leave, they also had a solution.

"Even if we cannot leave, passing the trial will draw the attention of the Ancestors who long left this world. While we don’t know if they are still alive, no matter the situation, passing the trial will send a signal to them, and they will return. Then we can think about what to do next.
But I doubt the Chaos Ascension King would go back on his word. He promised us our freedom as long as we could pass his trial," Tumenk answered, and Kent nodded.

"Regardless, even if the Universe rejects you, I have my own pocket dimension where the universe cannot reach. I will just stash you guys there until I can find a way to talk to the universe and negotiate on your behalf."
They smiled and nodded.
Honestly, Kent didn’t know if this was all part of his plan, but he now believed he was the Chaos Ascension King, and these people might just be an army he had prepared for this very moment.
As for what they were needed for, he could only hope he found out sooner because, if he were to be frank with himself, his mind was aching from thinking about everything.
He let out a sigh and then said,
"Please, kindly take me to the trial area. It has been 50 years already. Even if only 50 days have passed in my world, I have to go back home."
They nodded, and Parand spread her Flame Storm Domain. In no time, it covered 5 million light-years. Kent couldn’t feel or see it, but he knew she had already reached a very far end of the world.
The next moment, he found himself standing before a large temple, so large he had to lift his head just to see it in its entirety.
"Can’t say I am baffled by the sight of yet another temple, but damn, who built this beauty?" Kent exclaimed, mesmerized by the temple’s beauty.
’If I can take this into the tower, won’t it be great.
"The Chaos Ascension King built it entirely from Origin Jade. Imbued within each slab of jade is a trace of Origin Dao."
Kent raised his brow, then, with a wave, a statue standing to the side of the building vanished, appearing inside his Soul Universe.
"My wives and Legion need it."
If it were anybody else, perhaps the tribe leaders would have penalized them. But it was Kent, the person they were all counting on.
They moved, and a few minutes later, entered the temple, where a couple of people stood on the grounds, awaiting the arrival of the seven tribe leaders.

chapters.title: Chapter 1791: Temple Guardian
paragraphs: All eyes turned to Kent the moment they walked into the hall.
While he wasn’t the shortest, considering he was in his demi-human form, making him far taller than Fiannarel, he was the new face there, so everyone gathered fixed their gaze on him.
Kent also scanned the hall, noticing that the people there were divided into seven groups, each with a distinct appearance. This made him realize they were from the seven tribes.
Naturally, when they reached the center of the hall, the tribe leaders split up, each heading toward their tribesmen.

"Follow me," Jyoti Lata said, leading Kent toward the Red Bone Chaos Tribe. Fiannarel, who was supposed to go with the Obsidian Scale Chaos Tribe, followed Kent to the Red Bone Chaos Tribe, holding his hand.
Being clingy had always been her thing.

However, since she had missed Kent so much, she had become even more clingy. But who could blame her? She had given up hope of ever returning to the Infinity Universe or reuniting with her favorite baby brother.
So if fate had brought him back to her, letting him go again would be the last thing she would do.

Kent was led to the side of the Red Bone Chaos Tribe, where he immediately recognized some faces. Kwame and the rest of the elders he had met before he started his cultivation were present. Aside from them, there were others he didn’t know, but he knew they knew him.
After all, he had created many scenes over the past 50 years in their tribe.
"Glad to see you again, Kent Madson," Kwame said, his voice low but loud enough to reach everyone in the hall.
Kent smiled and replied,
"Good to be here, Lord Kwame."

Kwame nodded and turned to Fiannarel. "Pleased to meet the Obsidian Flame Archeress again. I apologize for not being there when you attained Eternity to congratulate you. That said, congratulations are in order."
Fiannarel nodded. "Thank you, Kwame."

Jyoti Lata sat in a throne-like chair and faced the other tribes, who were still looking at Kent. They all seemed curious to learn more about him, especially after witnessing the arrival of people different from them in the past.
Some turned out to be great people, while others perished due to their stupidity. Regardless, Kent was the fresh blood, and so they all wanted to know more about him.

The weakest person by the standards of the Chaos Chasm, excluding Kent, was a lad from the Storm Wing Chaos Tribe. However, even he was a True Supreme, something that would have made him a powerhouse in the Infinity Universe.
But while they would love to say Kent was the weakest, all of them could tell at a glance that the demigod dragon wasn’t simple at all.
If anything, the few Celestials among them could tell defeating him would be extremely tedious, perhaps even impossible.
So their interest in him seemed to grow by the second.
Jyoti Lata saw that, so she wasted no time.
"I know all of you are wondering who this person is," she said, her gaze sweeping across the room. "He is Kent Madson, a native of the Infinity Universe and Lady Fiannarel’s long-lost brother.

He appeared 50 years ago of his own accord, and since then, he has been training in the Red Bone Chaos Tribe, preparing to challenge the Chaos Ascension King Trial on behalf of the Red Bone Chaos Tribe.

Now, before I take all the credit, know that your various tribe leaders were present to assess and aid his growth, so whatever the results of this trial may be, Kent Madson will be someone welcome in all seven tribes... unless, of course, any of you have a problem with that."
Her calm gaze swept across the room, telling everyone to keep their complaints to themselves because she would not tolerate any arrogance.
Seeing nobody make a fuss, she continued...

"Good. Kent Madson would like to say a few words before we start the trial. Now, I would like to stress that, however things may turn out in the end, Kent Madson is a friend of ours, so he should be treated with respect."
The last thing she wanted was for their people to disrespect Kent, only to turn out to be the Chaos Ascension King.

"As Tribe Leader Jyoti Lata said, I will be challenging the Chaos Ascension King Trial. However, I have a request, and I do hope you all will accept it without complaint." Kent took a deep breath before making his request.

"I have already cultivated all seven techniques of the seven tribes, so my request is simple: when the trial opens, I will enter last. However, I want you all to enter one at a time, starting with the Void Vein Chaos Tribe." Many frowned, but Kent wasn’t done.

"Tribe Leader Jyoti Lata theorizes that the trials are based on the cultivation methods of the seven tribes. So I want to confirm it, and the only way to do so is to read the memories of those who will be challenging the trial."

"That is impossible, Kent Madson. The participants get their memories wiped before they are sent out, so you won’t be able to read their minds," a towering man with thick skin said, but Kent merely smiled.
"Leave that part to me. I have my ways of getting those memories back." His words were filled with confidence.
The tribe leaders with whom he had discussed this had always trusted and believed he could pull it off. So they quickly calmed everyone down.
Kent was still a mystery, so they wanted to see what he could do.

After everyone accepted Kent’s proposal, the seven tribe leaders retrieved an insignia and channeled their energies into it before letting it fly out of their hands. The insignias merged with a platform inside the hall, causing the entire temple to tremble.
Then, when the trembling calmed down, a voice spread throughout the temple, causing Kent to raise a brow.
"Welcome to the Chaos Ascension King Temple. I am the temple guardian, and yet again, I will see to it that this year’s Chaos Ascension King Trial proceeds smoothly."

The voice of the temple guardian was eerily similar to Tower’s, only this one sounded more mature. Kent wondered if it was merely his imagination, but he could tell that whoever this person was shared some connection with his dear Tower.

"I will open the trial now, and as always, the brave ones shall venture in and try their luck. The longer one stays inside, the more rewards one earns, so strive for more and, well, lose with dignity."
Kent smirked and watched as seven portals opened.
"Now, when you are ready."
Kent turned and looked at the representative of the Void Vein Chaos Tribe. He was a slender man with toned muscles and amber eyes.
He, of course, had silver skin like all members of the Void Vein Chaos Tribe. However, Kent could tell he was special. He just couldn’t put his finger on what made him special.
He nodded at the young man, and the young man nodded back.
Then, with calm steps, he walked into the portal.
Kent took a deep breath and was about to turn to Fiannarel when the person who had just walked in came flying back out as though he had been shot from a cannon.
"What the hell?" Kent exclaimed, but the rest of the people around him merely sighed, as though they had already expected this.

She had given up hope of ever returning to the Infinity Universe or reuniting with her favorite baby brother.
So if fate had brought him back to her, letting him go again would be the last thing she would do.
Kent was led to the side of the Red Bone Chaos Tribe, where he immediately recognized some faces.
Kwame and the rest of the elders he had met before he started his cultivation were present.
Aside from them, there were others he didn’t know, but he knew they knew him.
After all, he had created many scenes over the past 50 years in their tribe.
"Glad to see you again, Kent Madson," Kwame said, his voice low but loud enough to reach everyone in the hall.
Kent smiled and replied,
"Good to be here, Lord Kwame."
Kwame nodded and turned to Fiannarel.
"Pleased to meet the Obsidian Flame Archeress again.
I apologize for not being there when you attained Eternity to congratulate you.
That said, congratulations are in order."
Fiannarel nodded.
"Thank you, Kwame."
Jyoti Lata sat in a throne-like chair and faced the other tribes, who were still looking at Kent.
They all seemed curious to learn more about him, especially after witnessing the arrival of people different from them in the past.
Some turned out to be great people, while others perished due to their stupidity.
Regardless, Kent was the fresh blood, and so they all wanted to know more about him.
The weakest person by the standards of the Chaos Chasm, excluding Kent, was a lad from the Storm Wing Chaos Tribe.
However, even he was a True Supreme, something that would have made him a powerhouse in the Infinity Universe.
But while they would love to say Kent was the weakest, all of them could tell at a glance that the demigod dragon wasn’t simple at all.
If anything, the few Celestials among them could tell defeating him would be extremely tedious, perhaps even impossible.
So their interest in him seemed to grow by the second.
Jyoti Lata saw that, so she wasted no time.
"I know all of you are wondering who this person is," she said, her gaze sweeping across the room.
"He is Kent Madson, a native of the Infinity Universe and Lady Fiannarel’s long-lost brother.

He appeared 50 years ago of his own accord, and since then, he has been training in the Red Bone Chaos Tribe, preparing to challenge the Chaos Ascension King Trial on behalf of the Red Bone Chaos Tribe.

Now, before I take all the credit, know that your various tribe leaders were present to assess and aid his growth, so whatever the results of this trial may be, Kent Madson will be someone welcome in all seven tribes... unless, of course, any of you have a problem with that."
Her calm gaze swept across the room, telling everyone to keep their complaints to themselves because she would not tolerate any arrogance.
Seeing nobody make a fuss, she continued...
"Good.
Kent Madson would like to say a few words before we start the trial.
Now, I would like to stress that, however things may turn out in the end, Kent Madson is a friend of ours, so he should be treated with respect."
The last thing she wanted was for their people to disrespect Kent, only to turn out to be the Chaos Ascension King.
"As Tribe Leader Jyoti Lata said, I will be challenging the Chaos Ascension King Trial.
However, I have a request, and I do hope you all will accept it without complaint." Kent took a deep breath before making his request.
"I have already cultivated all seven techniques of the seven tribes, so my request is simple: when the trial opens, I will enter last.
However, I want you all to enter one at a time, starting with the Void Vein Chaos Tribe." Many frowned, but Kent wasn’t done.
"Tribe Leader Jyoti Lata theorizes that the trials are based on the cultivation methods of the seven tribes.
So I want to confirm it, and the only way to do so is to read the memories of those who will be challenging the trial."
"That is impossible, Kent Madson.
The participants get their memories wiped before they are sent out, so you won’t be able to read their minds," a towering man with thick skin said, but Kent merely smiled.
"Leave that part to me.
I have my ways of getting those memories back." His words were filled with confidence.
The tribe leaders with whom he had discussed this had always trusted and believed he could pull it off.
So they quickly calmed everyone down.
Kent was still a mystery, so they wanted to see what he could do.
After everyone accepted Kent’s proposal, the seven tribe leaders retrieved an insignia and channeled their energies into it before letting it fly out of their hands.
The insignias merged with a platform inside the hall, causing the entire temple to tremble.
Then, when the trembling calmed down, a voice spread throughout the temple, causing Kent to raise a brow.
"Welcome to the Chaos Ascension King Temple.
I am the temple guardian, and yet again, I will see to it that this year’s Chaos Ascension King Trial proceeds smoothly."
The voice of the temple guardian was eerily similar to Tower’s, only this one sounded more mature.
Kent wondered if it was merely his imagination, but he could tell that whoever this person was shared some connection with his dear Tower.
"I will open the trial now, and as always, the brave ones shall venture in and try their luck.
The longer one stays inside, the more rewards one earns, so strive for more and, well, lose with dignity."
Kent smirked and watched as seven portals opened.
"Now, when you are ready."
Kent turned and looked at the representative of the Void Vein Chaos Tribe.
He was a slender man with toned muscles and amber eyes.
He, of course, had silver skin like all members of the Void Vein Chaos Tribe.
However, Kent could tell he was special.
He just couldn’t put his finger on what made him special.
He nodded at the young man, and the young man nodded back.
Then, with calm steps, he walked into the portal.
Kent took a deep breath and was about to turn to Fiannarel when the person who had just walked in came flying back out as though he had been shot from a cannon.
"What the hell?" Kent exclaimed, but the rest of the people around him merely sighed, as though they had already expected this.

chapters.title: Chapter 1792: White Haired Fisherman
paragraphs: Kent was taken aback by how suddenly everything happened.

One moment, the representative from the Void Vein Chaos Tribe entered the portal; the next, he was flying back out as though he had been struck by a truck. The abruptness and shock of it all were simply mind-blowing.
The young man managed to stabilize himself before letting out a sigh.
"Well, that was uneventful," Kent said as he walked toward the young man, who wore a calm yet disappointed expression. He watched as the portal the young man had entered closed.
Kent stepped into his line of sight and took a deep breath.
"I suppose that means you failed?" he asked.
The young man, who went by the name Frafal, nodded. "I expected to last at least a minute, but I guess I wasn’t strong enough."
Kent raised a brow. "You make it sound like lasting a minute is a huge achievement."

In response, Jyoti Lata answered, "Actually, lasting even ten seconds is a great achievement. While we aspire to clear the trial and be free, we also know that whoever lasts the longest inside the trial will one day become a terrifying warrior of their respective tribe.
The reward the temple guardian spoke about is something innate. So, while he lasted just three seconds, his gains are akin to those of someone who has taken a Dao Transformation Pill."
Kent knitted his brows and sucked in a deep breath. "I know I’ll be shocked by the answer, but what is the highest recorded time?"
"Five minutes, and I hold that record," Fiannarel replied, a smile playing on her face.
Kent shook his head and nodded. "That is an eye-opener. I never expected there to be such a shocking side to the trial, but well... what the hell."
The tribe leaders sighed.
That was all they could do in this situation. Kent wasn’t familiar with the trial yet, so they wanted him to experience it.
They knew that even if he failed, 50,000 years later, he could try again. He would have three chances to test his luck, so they wanted to see what he could do.
"Whatever, now let me see what you saw."

Kent waved his hand, and two figures appeared before him. Lady Kenzie instantly filled the hall with flowers and butterflies, while off to the side, Death, whom Kent had chosen to call Hades, sat in a recliner with a hat covering his face.
While the appearance of the two made everyone suck in a cold breath, Kent grinned and smacked Hades on the leg.
"Stand up, sleepyhead. Time to do your thing."
Hades took offense as he slowly removed the hat from his face and glared at Kent.
"You would do well to behave around me, Dragon. My majestic self had been in chains for as long as I can remember... which isn’t a long time, but you get the idea."
Kent smirked. "You live with me now, so get to work, or I’ll cut off your supply of death energy and let you starve."
Hades didn’t want that to happen, so he jumped to his feet, walked toward Frafal, and pressed a finger against his forehead.
For a moment, nothing happened.
However, soon Frafal turned pale, and his body began to wither. Luckily, the Spirit of Life was there. Lady Kenzie extended her hand, and life essence poured into his body, healing him.
A few minutes later, Hades removed his finger from Frafal’s forehead and turned to Kent, pressing it against his forehead.
Kent felt a memory slip into his mind. He quickly accessed it, and that was when he saw what had happened.
Frafal stepped through the portal, and then he appeared on a small platform in front of a pond, or perhaps a river. The place was quiet and beautiful. Ahead of him, thirteen moons shone in the sky.
He admired the moon for only a second before his gaze shifted downward and landed on a figure seated on the platform, holding a fishing rod with its hook lowered into the water.
The person had his back turned to him. However, he could tell the person was a man, with silky white hair flowing down his back.
The man then spoke.
"So it has been 50,000 years already, huh?"
Frafal nodded and replied, "Yes, Senior. It has been 50,000 years, so I am here for my trial."
"Is that so?"
"Yes, Senior."
Frafal heard a hum come from the man. Then, the next second, he spoke.
"That is good. Unfortunately for you, the person I have been waiting for isn’t you. So go back and grow stronger, for he will need you."
The fishing rod rose from the water and landed on Frafal’s shoulder, sending him flying out of the portal.
Kent took a deep breath and smiled.
"Well then, it appears the trial isn’t as simple as we all thought."
"Little brother, were you able to extract anything?" Fiannarel asked.
"I did. However, let the others finish first just to be sure."
Thus, the other representatives from the remaining tribes began entering the trial one by one. However, just like Frafal, the moment they entered, they were thrown back out.
As they checked their memories, Kent saw the same scene play out for each of them. By the time the last person came out, Kent knew what awaited him.
But before he entered, he first revealed what he had seen in their memories.

"So, from what each of them experienced, it appears there is a mysterious white-haired fisherman waiting for someone inside the trial. Now, I am going to take a wild guess and say that he is the Chaos Ascension King.
That said, even if he turns out to be someone else, I will find out when I enter. There is a chance he may be waiting for someone worthy to pass a technique on to, and I might just be that person."
His last sentence was a bit arrogant, but considering everyone else had failed, he was their only hope now.

Fiannarel hugged Kent and said, "Be careful in there, little brother. If what you just said is true, then maybe you will fail. But knowing you, I am sure you will find a way to succeed, so good luck."
"I will give it my best, big sister," Kent said, and Fiannarel nodded.
"See you all later."
Kent smiled and walked toward the portal. Just before walking through it, he turned back to look at Fiannarel.
However, to everyone’s stunned gaze, a fishing hook shot out from the portal. The line wrapped itself around Kent’s horn, and before he knew it, he was dragged into the portal.
Many gasped, but there was nothing they could do except wait.
A second passed, and before long, five seconds went by, but Kent didn’t come flying back out as the others had.

A minute soon passed, but nothing happened. After five minutes, smiles started to appear on everyone’s faces. It was clear Kent wasn’t coming out anytime soon, which meant he seemed to be holding on just fine inside the trial.

Meanwhile, inside the trial, Kent appeared right where Frafal and the others had been when they entered. His gaze then landed on the mysterious fisherman, and for a moment, he wondered who the man was.
Then the fisherman spoke, and Kent’s eyes widened.
"Long time no see, Chaos Dragon."
The fisherman turned slightly to look at him.
"P-Paragon..."

chapters.title: Chapter 1793: Why...?
paragraphs: Somewhere deep within him, Kent suspected he would be meeting this person. Call it gut feeling or merely natural observation, but everything he had experienced had the Paragon’s fingerprints all over it.
However, he could also tell he wasn’t here because of the Paragon.
He could tell he had come here of his own accord; he just didn’t know whether it was due to his past incarnation or someone else entirely.
But after everything, he knew the Paragon was involved. After all, whenever he broke the rules to grow stronger, the Paragon always seemed to be there, making sure the laws stayed in their place.
Seeing the familiar face of the Paragon, Kent truly believed he might just be the good-looking one after all.
"Was the whole hook-to-horn thing really necessary?" He stood up and wiped the invisible dirt from his arm.

"You were taking too long to get here, so I had to hasten your pace," Paragon replied, throwing his fishing line back into the water. Kent smirked and walked to his side, and when he got close, a chair materialized out of thin air, and he sat on it.
Kent took his time, first examining his surroundings.
Aside from the river, which he knew contained no fish, there was also a vast forest around them, filled with what Kent could only describe as a wondrous miracle.
He could tell that the very air flowing through the shade of the trees was made up of all kinds of Laws, Daos, and even Eternal Laws.

It was as if the owner of this realm had imprisoned these Laws, making them nurture everything that came here. Seeing this, he finally understood why the longer one spent with her, the more powerful and full of potential they became.
It turned out that just by breathing here, one grew stronger. Kent was stunned by this, but what shocked him even more were the thirteen moons in the sky.
This came as a shock because inside his Tower, there were also thirteen moons, which he believed represented the thirteen lives he had lived. So if that was the case, didn’t this mean he was...
"So I am the Chaos Ascension King, huh?" he asked, and Paragon smirked.
"Obviously. It is sad you never realized this from the beginning." Paragon said with a chuckle...

"But how? Usually, when I get to an unfamiliar yet familiar place, it triggers my memories. The only trigger I got upon coming here was that of my incarnation who lived during the Sun Era, and it had nothing to do with me being the Chaos Ascension King. So how is that possible?"
He took a deep breath and asked a direct question. "Is the Chaos Ascension King one of my thirteen incarnations?"
"No," Paragon replied, turning to look at Kent. "The Chaos Ascension King is you, the real you..."
"The real me. I don’t understand."

Paragon smiled and answered, "Of course you don’t. None of this makes any sense, and I cannot interfere with your life, so I cannot say much. But know this: a very long time ago, I assembled a team of seven powerful warriors, of whom you were a part.
Our mission concerned the fate of Existence. And when I say Existence, I mean everything. The planets, galaxies, universes, and multiverses... everything that is known and yet to be known.
The mission was simple: save Existence from something far more dreadful. We fought, and we failed. Terribly, really. We were trashed beyond repair...hehe"
Kent furrowed his brow, a bit amused. "Are you saying there was someone more dreadful than you, the Paragon?"
Paragon smirked, also amused by what Kent had said. "Let’s not stray away from the topic. So we lost, but we didn’t, because before it could end for us, we got a second chance from an unlikely ally.
This person gave us a chance to start over again, but this time, on our own terms. I am the Paragon, so naturally, I was the perfect person to make sure you seven didn’t stray from your path.

To win, we all had to become the best of the best. We already were, but we weren’t the best, considering we came close to dying. But this time, things will be different because, guess what, you have a Paragon on your team."
Kent smirked, knowing Paragon was merely blowing his own horn. But he allowed himself to entertain the idea that, a very long time ago, the eight of them had faced an existence they couldn’t defeat.

If that was the case, then just what was that existence, and how powerful did they have to be to stop it? Most importantly, what did a person have to do to become one of the best, someone worthy to be a part of such a team?
"Tell me something, Paragon. Looking at me now, do you think I am on the right path, or am I still lacking?"
"The fact that you are here now, seated beside me as a demigod with the power of a Celestial, shows you are on the right path. You are the Primordial Chaos Dragon, buddy.
Your existence is as unbelievable as mine. The only difference between us is that I have no home, but you do, and you have the fate of all Existence behind you."

Paragon smiled and added, "But we have to do better. We have to reach the peak before he awakens. We failed once simply because we underestimated our opponent. But like you always say, there is nothing in Existence or above Existence that cannot be killed.

So, Master of Chaos, now that your journey has finally begun, do well to rise to the occasion, for I have already reached the stage we should be at, and I believe you and the others will too, eventually."
"And where is that stage? Which stage will make me someone worthy to stand between whatever wants to devour Existence and not break out in a cold sweat?"
Paragon chuckled, almost laughing at Kent’s question.

"You know, sometimes I forget you are someone very manipulative, Chaos Dragon. The first time we met, you had just become a Celestial with power that rivaled Eternals. Of course, I knew you still had more to learn, but I underestimated how cunning a dragon could be."

Paragon laughed and added, "You can ask all the questions you want, Kent, but we both know I will not answer you, else I risk ruining everything for you. Some knowledge is meant to be discovered naturally.
So maybe now that you have everything, challenge yourself and rise above all threats. Your universe is in grave danger, so while you may feel like a powerhouse now, don’t underestimate anyone."
Kent smirked and took a deep breath, knowing he had already heard all he had to know.
"Why do I feel like when I return to my universe, my life will be one chaotic moment after another?"

"You are the Primordial Chaos Dragon, so what do you expect? But that is true. Your peaceful days are coming to an end. In fact, I waited for you here to grant you the opportunity to handle one of those threats." Paragon waved his hand, and a scene appeared before Kent.
The scene showed death and destruction scattered across millions of planets.

"This is your universe 10,000 years from today. Something will come up, and you will be unavailable, or more accurately, occupied. During that time, the Dark Empress will attack with her Dark Fiends, and this will be the result.
But I can grant you the chance to kill her today, if you are up for it."

But like you always say, there is nothing in Existence or above Existence that cannot be killed.

So, Master of Chaos, now that your journey has finally begun, do well to rise to the occasion, for I have already reached the stage we should be at, and I believe you and the others will too, eventually."
"And where is that stage?
Which stage will make me someone worthy to stand between whatever wants to devour Existence and not break out in a cold sweat?"
Paragon chuckled, almost laughing at Kent’s question.
"You know, sometimes I forget you are someone very manipulative, Chaos Dragon.
The first time we met, you had just become a Celestial with power that rivaled Eternals.
Of course, I knew you still had more to learn, but I underestimated how cunning a dragon could be."
Paragon laughed and added, "You can ask all the questions you want, Kent, but we both know I will not answer you, else I risk ruining everything for you.
Some knowledge is meant to be discovered naturally.
So maybe now that you have everything, challenge yourself and rise above all threats.
Your universe is in grave danger, so while you may feel like a powerhouse now, don’t underestimate anyone."
Kent smirked and took a deep breath, knowing he had already heard all he had to know.
"Why do I feel like when I return to my universe, my life will be one chaotic moment after another?"
"You are the Primordial Chaos Dragon, so what do you expect?
But that is true.
Your peaceful days are coming to an end.
In fact, I waited for you here to grant you the opportunity to handle one of those threats." Paragon waved his hand, and a scene appeared before Kent.
The scene showed death and destruction scattered across millions of planets.
"This is your universe 10,000 years from today.
Something will come up, and you will be unavailable, or more accurately, occupied.
During that time, the Dark Empress will attack with her Dark Fiends, and this will be the result.
But I can grant you the chance to kill her today, if you are up for it."

chapters.title: Chapter 1794: The Trial
paragraphs: During the Dark Era, when the Dark Creatures attacked, everyone fought bravely, and they won in the end... well, that was the narrative they believed.
However, that narrative was far from the truth.

In fact, the truth was that during the battle, when the Ruthless Bandit and the Night Riders faced off against the Dark Empress, the true Dark Empress remained hidden in a corner, waiting for the battle to end so she could make her debut.
Her plan was simple: while everyone had their guard lowered, she would make her move...
However, one spell from the Ruthless Bandit prevented her from accomplishing that, and so, since the Dark Era, she had been biding her time to return and exact her revenge.
Kent was already aware of her return.
He had already started making plans to handle her growing threat. Never did he expect that not only would he fail, but he wouldn’t even be there to handle it.
He could only wonder what was so important that it would make him miss such a clash. This also made him wonder just how powerful the Dark Empress had become after lying dormant for many eras.
He really had to put an end to her growing threat quickly before things became even more dire.
"Of course, I will take her on and squash her like a bug. But tell me, how strong is she right now?"
"If only her individual strength is put into question, then she isn’t that strong. But she is the Dark Empress with millions of Dark Fiends. This makes her a terror that cannot be underestimated.

Right now, you can kill her, but it will depend on how you approach it. All I can do is open the path for you and give you one last boost, since from here onward, your path will depend on your own decisions."
Kent nodded. "Then I will take on the mission. However, I have a question regarding the freedom I promised the people in the Chaos Chasm. If I finish this trial, can I free them from this place?"
"How should I know?" Paragon smirked.
"The last I checked, you created them, so do with them as you please. I just know that this world is your creation for a specific reason.

The people in it are also your creation for some top-level mission you never told me about. So maybe when you are done with the trial, that mission will reveal itself. But as far as I am concerned, their fate is in your hands now."
Kent sat frozen, unsure of what to say. But Paragon wasn’t done, not even by a long shot...

"But you must know, they cannot appear in your universe, at least not as Primordials or Eternals. Even if one Eternal were to step foot there, your universe will become a target for a higher form of war, one you are not ready for.
So, unless they are willing to submit to the Universe and have their cultivation base suppressed to the Celestial stage, then fine, you can send them there.
But then again, you told me they are your creation, part of a mission that will determine the fate of your universe. So maybe meet that lady first, and the rest will come to you eventually."
Kent nodded and asked, "Which lady should I meet?"
"I believe you used to call her Tower. I wonder why you gave such a name to someone so important to you."

Paragon suddenly swung his arm, and the fishing line stretched, showing it had latched onto something. With one pull, the water parted, and a large gate rose from the depths. It stopped, splashing water everywhere.
"There is no trial, but more of a mission. That said, it has become a trial now, and through this portal, you will be taken to where you will understand the core details of this unique realm.
I left this mark here today to help you break the rules twice. The first is the Dark Empress. Killing her now will be hard, but with this, I believe you can pull it off."
Paragon flicked his hand, and an orb flew over and merged with Kent’s forehead.
<You have received a Limitless Technique: Omnipresent Universe Three Body Art>
The details of the technique flowed into Kent’s mind...
"I will be leaving for now. Maybe one day, we will meet again, and hopefully, when that time comes, you will be done with the matters in your Universe and have ventured into the Universe Ocean."

The fishing line turned into sparks of light alongside Paragon, who disappeared, leaving Kent to ponder everything he had just heard. More importantly, he could now focus on the trial that had turned into a fight against a universe-level threat.
"An existence that even the Paragon couldn’t handle, huh... Makes me wonder just how powerful such a person really is," he smiled and chose to calm his heart for now.
The day would come when he would see who they were going up against. Hopefully, when that day finally arrived, he would be able to handle it.

He also pondered the fact that he had created the Chaos beings in the Chaos Chasm. Honestly, he wasn’t too shocked by that, since it had crossed his mind the moment he discovered he was the Chaos Ascension King.
But knowing he was the progenitor of such a powerful race made him wonder just what he had planned for them. His mind was filled with so many questions, but he allowed himself to relax.

He took a step forward and entered the gateway that Paragon had dragged from the water. The next second, he appeared in a hall identical to the one he, the seven tribe leaders, and Fiannarel had come to for the Chaos Ascension King Trial.
Well, it appeared this place might be the real temple, since the one who had spoken to them as the Temple Guardian now stood facing him.
Their gazes met, and although this figure stood 5’9" tall, she looked exactly like Tower. She smiled and said, "Welcome back, Master. I have been expecting you."
Kent was stunned for a few moments before asking,
"Are you Tower?"
She smiled and replied, "Yes. I am the real deal, the true Tower."
"How is that possible?"

"My job is to make sure the Master grows stronger and to aid in any way I can to ensure the Universe is protected. I have been guarding the Master’s legacy ever since you chose to pursue true reincarnation.

I had to ensure your legacy remained intact while also protecting the race you had left behind. So, I extracted two parts of my existence and let one escort you through the thirteen cycles of reincarnation while the other protected the Chaos Chasm.
As for me, my main mission is to hold on to this." She extended her hand, and a book of about three hundred pages was placed into Kent’s hands. He reached for it with steady hands.
"What is it?" Kent asked, looking at the book. He tried to open it, but it was sealed.
"It contains the account of who you were, why you became the Primordial Chaos Dragon and what you plan to do from this moment onward."
Kent examined the book a few more times before asking again, "How do I open it?"
"Master cannot open it just like that. The pages will open for you when the time is right. For now, the Master should follow me to where we can begin the legacy inheritance."
